articleTitle: Forecasting Generating Power of Sun Tracking PV Plant using Long-Short Term Memory Neural Network Model: A case study in Ninh Thuan - Vietnam
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This article provides a reliable very short-term forecast (nowcasting) of the power generation capacity of PV power plants. Specifically, in this article, a deep learning method utilized the long-short term memory model (LSTM) to predict PV system’s power generation has been proposed using the Python programming language with TensorFlow library. In addition, other deep learning models such as recurrent neural network (RNN) and convolution neural network (CNN) are also used and compared with LSTM to demonstrate the advantages of LSTM compared to those models. To verify, the article used actual data collected from Ninh Thuan solar power plant - Vietnam. The results show the prediction ability with promising quality of the LSTM model.

articleTitle: Mutual Impacts of Different Dead-times and Control Sample Times on SiC Inverter Loss in Experimental Motor Drive at High Carrier Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: At high pulse-width modulation (PWM) carrier frequencies up to 200 kHz using silicon carbide (SiC) devices, the individual and mutual impacts of the sample time and dead-time on the SiC inverter loss in a motor drive system may become significantly. Thus, these issues under load condition are experimentally investigated and analyzed in the present study, where the dead-time is from 250 to 1000 ns and the control sample time is from 100 to 1000 μs. Furthermore, the measured results with the SiC metal–oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) inverter are briefly compared to that with the silicon (Si) insulated-gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) inverter for reference. Moreover, the total harmonics distortion (THD) of the measured voltage and current of the considered interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) is provided to explain the results. Finally, insights with theoretical analysis are shown as complementary explanations of the experimental findings. The outcome of this research can be treated as a reference in choosing the suitable value of the control sample time for IPMSM drive systems using SiC-MOSFET inverters.

articleTitle: Current Feedback Method - A New Approach of Field-Weakening Control for Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In the realm of electric propulsion and industrial automation, the increase in motor performance has led to the development of advanced control techniques. Among these, field-weakening control stands out as a pivotal strategy for extending the operational envelope of electric motors beyond their nominal speed range. This research investigates a simple but effective field-weakening strategy applied for the three-phase surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) based on the characteristic of q-axis current at a high-speed region. The conventional proportional-integral (PI) controller computes the appropriate reference d-axis current via the error between the reference and estimated values of the q-axis current. In addition, the parameters of the PI controller are determined by the Particle-Swarm-Optimization algorithm concerning minimizing the difference in rotor speed and q-axis current. The performance of the proposed strategy is evaluated by the software simulation in MATLAB/Simulink. The proposed field-weakening strategy can be used in other electric motor types.

articleTitle: Hybrid Orthogonal-Nonorthogonal Multiple Access for CR-Assisted Cooperative UAV Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Non-terrestrial networks based on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are considered for integration with 6G mobile networks to provide ubiquitous communication through heterogeneous networks. UAVs offer benefits such as flexible deployment, mobility control, and strong line-of-sight links. In this paper, orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) are combined to form a hybrid OMA-NOMA cognitive radio (CR) assisted cooperative UAV system. The selection of either the OMA or NOMA mode is carried out such that the best link quality is offered to the user equipments (UEs) compared to the individual modes. In this system, the base station uses the NOMA mode for the transmission to the UAVs which act as decode-and-forward relays each serving a cluster of UEs. The CR paradigm is used for the NOMA mode of the hybrid system to reduce the interference caused by the UAVs to adjacent clusters of UEs. Analytical expressions of the outage probability and sum rate of the OMA, NOMA, and hybrid OMA-NOMA systems are derived. Numerical results are provided to reveal the performance advantages of the proposed hybrid OMA-NOMA CR-assisted cooperative UAV system over Nakagami-m fading. Further, design options and tradeoffs between the OMA, NOMA, and hybrid OMA-NOMA systems are illustrated.

articleTitle: ECG-based Cardiovascular Disease Classification using Modified Inception
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are appearing more and more frequently. There is a growing concern about the severity of these diseases. Medical practitioners normally utilize Electrocardiogram (ECG) to detect onset of the disease and give initial diagnosis. Unfortunately, it is costly and laborious for the medical practitioners to analyze a large amount of ECG data. Current methods still lack performance across different recording sessions. On the other hand, manual evaluation ECG signals is a big challenge for inexperienced cardiologists. Recently, application of Deep Learning in ECG-based cardiac disease classification has been achieved. Its performance now is reaching that of the cardiologists. In this paper, a new method to classify ECG-based CVD diseases is proposed . The original ECG signals are transformed into 2D domain and classified by a modified Inception model. The experiments show that the proposed method attains satisfactory performance surpassing recent works.

articleTitle: A Dataset and Quality Evaluation of AI-generated Images for Online Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: AI-generated content is becoming an integral part of online education. Researchers have made efforts to examine the influence of such content on user satisfaction by creating AI-generated datasets and conducting subjective experiments. While several existing datasets cover various aspects of human life, we have developed the first AI-generated image (AIGI) dataset specifically for online learning. Also, we conducted a crowd-based subjective experiment to obtain human ratings for both perceptual and alignment assessments of the AIGIs. Using the new dataset as a benchmark, we carried out an evaluation of a large number of quality models. In contrast to previous studies, the results in this study showed that existing quality models are not effective yet in predicting quality of the images in online learning.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Fabry-Perot Antenna With High Isolation and Wideband RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we investigates a Fabry-Perot antenna (FPA) with dual-polarization, low coupling coefficient, and wideband radar cross section (RCS) reduction. Fabry-Perot cavity is constructed by a copper-plate as ground (GND) below a single-layer partially reflecting surface (PRS). The PRS is a combination of strips array on the top side and a cross-slot array on the bottom side. While the former operates as chessboard arrangement metasurface (CAMs) to reduce RCS, the latter yields high reflection coefficient for gain enhancement. Feed antenna placed in the center of GND contains a square patch fed by 4 T-shaped feeding networks. The proposed antenna achieves a very high port-to-port isolation by remaining the symmetry structure across two planes and the support of double differential-feed. Its 3 dB gain bandwidths are 5.63-6.29 GHz, 5.78-6.23 GHz with the highest value of 12.5 dBi, 15 dBi for port 1 and 2, respectively. Also, it achieves a wide RCS reduction bandwidth of 66.7% (4.5−9.0 GHz).

articleTitle: Switching Control of Transmitting Lane Sections in Dynamic Wireless Charging System for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: To reduce the magnetic field radiation and power loss in dynamic wireless charging systems for electric vehicles, the power is supplied only to the section of the transmitting lane where the electric vehicle is passing through, rather than to the entire transmitting lane. This paper proposes a new approach for controlling the switching of transmitting lane sections based on the position of electric vehicles. The proposed method only requires measuring current on coils below the transmitting lane to locate electric vehicles, negating the need for additional sensors or cameras. Moreover, the switching control position is selected to minimize the power pulsation of the load. The study shows that the position of the electric vehicle is accurately detected, and the power pulse rate is 5.8%.

articleTitle: Reach on Fuzzy Logic Control for Electric Power Steering System
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This article presents a technique that uses fuzzy logic control (FL) to regulate a 3-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor to meet the requirements of electric power steering across different road speeds and circumstances. The proposed FL controller demonstrates robust performance in regulating the PMSM motor for electric power steering applications. By incorporating FOC and sensor feedback, the system effectively adjusts the motor voltage to provide the necessary steering assistance across varying driving conditions. The MATLAB simulation results validate the system's ability to meet the stringent performance criteria of electric power steering systems, ensuring a seamless and responsive steering experience for drivers. The electric power steering system suggested provides smooth steering from 0km/h to 120km/h, with power steering torque ranging from 20,71 Nm to 15,7 Nm. The precision and efficacy of the solution are confirme by MATLAB simulation, verifying its ability to fulfill the demanding performance standards of electric power steering systems.

articleTitle: Maximizing Mutual Information for Covert Sensing in Joint Radar-Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: While traditionally radar and communication systems have operated independently, in-depth research has revealed that combining them can lead to significant advantages. This combined approach offers an improvement in overall system functionality by simplifying structures, reducing hardware usage, enhancing efficiency, mitigating electromagnetic interference, etc. In this paper, we formulate an optimization scheme for a joint radar and communication (JRC) system that allows the Radar to simultaneously estimate channel parameters from the target returns and decode the received communications signals. The primary objective is to maximize the mutual information (MI) exchange by optimizing the Radar’s transmit power while guaranteeing a predefined threshold data rate for data transmission and the desired threshold for covertness requirement. Numerical results show that the Radar can effectively adjust its transmit power to successfully hide its presence from the target up to over ninety percent and also meet the minimum requirement of information rate.

articleTitle: A Design Of Intelligent Reflecting Surface Using Spidron Structure For 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs), which are 2-D structures comprising numerous unit cells, have emerged as one of the pivotal technologies for the sixth generation (6G) of wireless communication networks. By dynamically tuning the amplitude and phase shift of each unit cell, IRSs provide an opportunity to reshape and control the reflective wave. For this reason, we can convert propagation environment into part of the network design parameters that are subject to optimization. In this paper we presents design of an IRS using spirdron structure for 6G applications. Firstly, we provide requirements of designing a new IRS in three key metrics, including unit-cell size, number of unit cell states, and IRS panel size. And then, a genetic algorithm is used for calculating the desired beam directions which are engineered with the proper phase states of each unit cell. Subsequently, a novel spidron structure is designed for 2-bit unit cell of IRS with size of 0.33λ × 0.33λ a 2.6 GHz. Thank to spidron shape, the features of IRS include light weight, wide scanning angle, and high scan resolution. For demonstration, an IRS panel with 34×10 cells are computationally investigated and the simulations result in a scan resolution of 10° and scan angle up to ±60° with peak gain of 22.6 dBi.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wide Range Refractive Index PCF-Based SPR Sensor for Lab-on-Chip Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Using finite element method, a novel photonic crystal fiber (PCF) based surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor, capable of detecting multiple samples simultaneously, is designed and analyzed in this paper. Applying perfectly matched layer boundary condition, maximum wavelength sensitivity of 22,000 nm/RIU, amplitude sensitivity of 1629 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">- 1</sup> and an ultra-wide range refractive index (RI) from 1.17 to <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.43,</inf> are reported for detecting gaseous and liquid materials. These features will open to design, analyze, fabricate, and test Lab-on-Chip (LOC) devices for plant science, food safety, environment analysis, and medical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Design of a Planar Transformer for Bidirectional Resonant Type Converters in On-Board Charger Applications: A Methodological Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Bidirectional DC−DC converters have gained prominence, particularly in on-board charger applications, with two candidates being the CLLC and Dual-Active Bridge (DAB) converters. While both options exist, the DAB converters face challenges associated with turning off at the peak current and uncertainty in achieving soft-switching under light load conditions, significantly impacting overall system efficiency. Consequently, this paper favors the CLLC converter. With the emerging wide bandgap devices, which enables a substantial increase in switching frequency, reaching several hundred kilohertz. This advancement facilitates the adoption of planar magnetic by using the printed circuit board (PCB) winding. In contrast to traditional litz wire-based transformers, planar transformers not only contribute to a reduction in converter size but also enhance system reliability through automated manufacturing processes that ensure predictability and repeatability of parasitic elements. Furthermore, the integration of leakage inductance into the transformer through flexible winding techniques reduces the need for additional magnetic components. This paper introduces an integrated magnetic method featuring controllable leakage inductance. In contrast to conventional methods, the integration cost is associated with core loss rather than copper loss, simplifying thermal management. The proposed design is implemented in a 3.5 kW CLLC converter, demonstrating a maximum transformer calculated efficiency of 99.2% and an overall estimated efficiency peak of 98.2%.

articleTitle: High Step-down Two-stage DC/DC Converter for Low Voltage Battery Charger
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In electric vehicles (EVs), low-voltage DC/DC battery chargers (LDCs) play a critical role in addressing the rising power demands in EVs. This paper studies a two-stage DC/DC converter design, combining a Buck converter and an LLC converter to effectively power the modern 800V EV battery. The converter aims to deliver 3.5kW at 13.6V, serving the high-power requirements of EV appliances such as sound system, display system, and air conditioning system. The first stage, a Buck converter, employs Discontinuous Conduction Mode (DCM), featuring a simple switch and diode configuration to reduce losses. The second stage, an LLC converter, operates at its resonant frequency to achieve optimal efficiency, utilizing an asymmetric half-bridge topology. Detailed analysis of the selected topology and transformer design, along with simulation results, are provided to validate the proposed system's efficacy.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of EMI Magnetic Shielding Approaches for Power Module
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Power modules have emerged as vital components in various applications where components are closely packed. The influence of magnetic fields on sensitive circuits is a crucial concern. This paper investigates the magnetic field coupling in the power module, presenting a comprehensive way to analysis the magnetic field coupling influence and proposing the usage of a magnetic shield to reduce the magnetic field coupling effect. The study obverse some characteristics of the magnetic shields and use a simple experiment to illustrate the characteristics of magnetic shield and provides some considerations to reduce the magnetic field coupling effect in the power module.

articleTitle: NOMA and IRS-assisted Secure UAV Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: With the advantages of intelligent reflecting surface (IRS), we consider an IRS-assisted unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) secure communication system, in which multiple ground users (GUs) are served by the UAV in the presence of a ground eavesdropper. We adopt the non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) technique to access GUs. The phase shift matrix of IRS, the trajectory, and transmit power of the UAV are jointly optimized to maximize the GUs’ average secrecy rate. However, this problem is highly intractable due to its non-convexity. Therefore, we first divide the formulated problem into three subproblems using the alternating optimization technique. Then, we transform the subproblems into solvable ones by utilizing successive convex approximation and semidefinite relaxation methods. Finally, we develop an effective algorithm to obtain the solution. Simulation results indicate that our scheme can achieve better performance gains compared to the baseline schemes.

articleTitle: An Innovative Pipeline For Corrosion Segmentation in Telecommunication Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The detection of corrosion on metallic structures plays a crucial role in timely maintenance as corrosion can lead to major safety risks. However, developing an own corrosion detection application faces some challenges in datasets: the lack of available datasets, or unsuitable with specific problems. In this work, we proposed a quick, efficient, easy-to-use pipeline to segment datasets based on color filters. After obtaining a dataset consisting of 612 images annotated with mask corrosion, we experimented with this dataset on different segmentation models and achieved an mIoU score of 0.8664 with OCRNet.

articleTitle: Sino-Vietnamese Text Transcription using Word Embedding Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Sino-Vietnamese (aka Han Viet) characters, derived from ancient Chinese script, held prominence in Vietnam for centuries until the advent of the modern scripting system. Despite their historical significance, contemporary Vietnamese struggle to decipher these characters, hindering access to valuable cultural artifacts. This paper explores the complexities of Sino-Vietnamese characters, their divergence from modern Chinese characters, and the intricate process of converting them into readable texts. Notably, Sino-Vietnamese characters boast eight tones compared with Mandarin’s five, adding to their linguistic complexity. While remnants of these characters persist in artifacts and bibliographies, their comprehension requires linguistic expertise because of the multiple possible readings for a single character. Addressing this challenge requires the development of tools for automatic recognition and translation, enabling broader access to Vietnam’s cultural heritage. By facilitating the understanding of ancient texts, these efforts have contributed to the preservation and appreciation of Vietnamese linguistic and cultural traditions.

articleTitle: Optimization of High-Efficiency Region of EV Traction Motor through Innovative Motor Constant Considering the Current Angle and Iron Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel definition of motor constants that integrates iron loss, current angle, and copper loss, providing a comprehensive assessment of motor performance and efficiency. By incorporating this innovative motor constant into the optimization process, multi-objective optimization becomes more streamlined, leading to enhanced motor designs with expanded high-efficiency operational ranges. The Genetic Algorithm (GA) optimization approach employed in this study, utilizing the new motor constant with the current angle as the fitness function, enables the identification of optimal parameters for the motor stator to maximize the high-efficiency operational range in the field weakening (FW) region. The analyses uncover a significant correlation between the new motor constant and efficiency, considering the influence of the current angle to achieve broader high-efficiency operational ranges. The electromagnetic properties of the designed motors are thoroughly examined and validated using finite element analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: Effects of Variety of Dynamic Facial Expressions on Attractiveness Judgments with Successive Viewing on Digital Media
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: It is widely known in laboratory experiments and everyday life that smiling increases attractiveness. However, negative facial expressions, such as angry faces, may also act as an indicator of honesty in certain situations and may increase facial attractiveness. While facial emotions are now relatively easy to simulate in various digital visual media, how facial expressions lead to the attractiveness of a person (or an avatar) remains largely unclear. In the present study, we examined whether judgments of facial attractiveness would depend solely on the positivity/negativity and frequency of expressions. Participants rated the attractiveness of faces with neutral facial expressions in static images before and after observing the dynamic facial expressions. One-third of the faces appeared twice as a smiling face (Two Smile condition), another third appeared twice as an angry face (Two Angry condition), and the remaining third appeared once as a smiling face and once as an angry (One Each condition). The results showed that the attractiveness ratings of the static face images were higher in the Two Smile and One Each conditions than in the Two Angry condition, but there was no significant difference between the Two Smile and One Each conditions. An additional analysis showed that changes in attractiveness were significantly greater when the participant and the face being rated were different genders. These results are partially consistent with the hypothesis that facial expressiveness, or the variety of facial expressions, may act as an honest signal and increase facial attractiveness. Our findings may also have implications for producing more attractive characters in avatars and robots.

articleTitle: Maximizing the Multi-User Downlink Transmission Rate in RIS-Assisted UAV System
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In future 6G mobile communication systems, the use of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) in conjunction with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) is leveraged to enhance air-to-ground communication system transmission performance. In this paper, the downlink of the RIS-assisted UAV communication system is considered, where the RIS is mounted beneath the UAV, allowing the downlink signals to be reflected from a multi-antenna base station through the RIS to multiple terminal devices. To enhance the system’s panoramic beamforming capability and maximize the total downlink transmission bits, an efficient alternating descent algorithm is proposed in this paper. This algorithm jointly optimizes the phase shift of the RIS and the transmit beamforming of the base station. The simulation results indicate that the algorithm proposed in this paper outperforms schemes that only optimize the phase shift of the RIS or the transmit beamforming of the base station in terms of system performance.

articleTitle: Circulating Tumor Cell (CTC) Separation from Blood Constituents Using A Dielectrophoresis-Based Microdevice
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Numerous studies have focused on circulating tumor cell separation, given its pivotal role in cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment. This study presents an effective microfluidic system that integrates a specialized dielectrophoresis structure, namely the facing-electrode configuration dielectrophoresis (FEC-DEP) structure, to isolate circulating tumor cells from various blood constituents, including red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. The FEC-DEP structure comprises a bottom slanted electrode array positioned parallel to a basic rectangular top electrode. These parallel electrodes generate a dielectrophoresis-induced non-homogeneous electric field. Therefore, when the FEC-DEP is integrated into a flow, it can guide different objects in the flow along distinct trajectories. Consequently, objects with similar characteristics can move together within the same stream. This design has the potential to reduce reliance on particle position within the microchannel and streamline the microfabrication process. The finite element method was employed for numerical analysis of the separation process, and device parameters were adjusted to optimize performance. The results demonstrate the ability of the microfluidic device to efficiently enrich tumor cells, achieving a high efficiency rate of approximately 80%, in a label-free and cost-effective manner.

articleTitle: A novel modeling and control design for a 3-phase Current-fed Dual Active Bridge converter in an AC Battery application
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the 3-phase Current-fed Dual active bridge (3P-CFDAB) converter in an AC Battery application due to its high power rate and efficiency. In this research, firstly, a small signal model for the 3P-CFDAB is designed in discharging mode. Secondly, the control structure for this converter is proposed in this mode, to support the grid at peak load or even grid blackout. Finally, the small signal model is verified by the multitone analysis by PLECS while the control design is performed with an additional soft-start procedure by MATLAB/ SIMULINK. The simulation results show a good agreement with the theoretical analysis.

Author Keywords: 3-phase Current- fed Dual active bridge (3P-CFDAB) converter

articleTitle: A Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna With Vertical Polarization For 5G Indoor Access Points
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents a vertically-polarized pattern-reconfigurable antenna for use in 5G indoor access points. The proposed design is comprised of a printed monopole loaded with four parasitic strips which are connected or disconnected from the ground plane (GND) by switching ON/OFF modes of pm diodes. By moderating connection/disconnection between the strips and GND the antenna obtains an omnidirectional and multibeam endfire radiation patterns. To enhance the impedance matching, a ring slot is etched on the GND. For verification, an antenna prototype operating at 3.6 GHz has been fabricated and measured. The prototype achieves an overlapped bandwidth from 3.20 to 3 85 GHz (18%) for all operating modes which cover 5G n77/n78 bands. For the far field, the antenna yields switched beam flexibility in the full azimuth plane. With the features of simple configuration, broadband and pattern reconfigurability, the proposed antenna is good candidate for use in 5G indoor access points.

articleTitle: Analysis of Input Voltage-Output Frequency Relationship in VCOs Using a Linear Time-Varying Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper delves into the dynamic behavior and control complexities of voltage-controlled oscillators (VCOs) within high-speed data transmission systems. We conduct an in-depth analysis of the intricate dynamics inherent to VCOs, recognizing their nonlinear nature. To accurately capture these nonlinearities and dynamic characteristics, we meticulously develop a comprehensive state-space model. Furthermore, we investigate the evolution of the linear time-varying (LTV) model from nonlinear models, particularly concerning specific voltage inputs. Our study also proposes a frequency calculation formula for computing the LTV model of the VCO, facilitating the design of control inputs. These advancements hold significant potential to enhance VCO performance in high-speed data transmission applications, offering valuable insights for further research and practical implementation.

articleTitle: A Power-Efficient Transmitter Design for 3D-Stacked Memories in 28-nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: High-bandwidth memory (HBM) interfaces are critical components in future computing systems, demanding both high data rates and energy efficiency. In this work, we introduce an energy-efficient transmitter design for HBM I/O interfaces using advanced 28-nm CMOS technology. The proposed HBM transmitter design could minimize the power consumption of the I/O interface across multi-drop through-silicon via (TSV) channels. We propose a novel dual-edge boosted pre-driver circuit that significantly enhances the slew rate and maintains signal integrity under severe process-voltage-temperature (PVT) variations. Through the simulation of a 12-stacked TSV channel with a total capacitance of 1 pF, the proposed transmitter is validated with a power consumption of 2.18 mW, achieving a data rate of 11 Gb/s. The energy efficiency of our transmitter reaches 0.198 pJ/b/pF, presenting a promising solution for an energy-efficient and high-speed HBM I/O interface.

articleTitle: A Novel Autorec-Based Architecture for Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, collaborative filtering systems based on neural networks have strides in delivering users with personalized recommendations. CI-Autorec accepts a range of content-based representations as input to enhance system efficiency. Sparse Autoencoder has been proven to synthesize and reduce computational costs while still delivering high-quality results. This paper presents a framework that leverages the content-based information utilization capabilities of the CI-Autorec and employs active units to predict of the Spare Autoencoder. Experimental trials demonstrate the advanced performance of our recommendation system against that of other combined systems.

articleTitle: An improved neural network algorithm for efficient scheduling of distributed energy resources in microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The promotion of environmental sustainability and pollution reduction has been facilitated by microgrids based on renewable energy sources (RESs). In microgrids that have multiple energy resources and storage systems, optimal scheduling is critical to maximizing power sharing between components and ensuring efficiency, reliability, and economical operation. This research aims to find the optimal generation strategy of different distributed energy resources (DERs) and energy storage system (ESS) based on an improved neural network algorithm (INNA) to minimize the generation cost of the microgrid. INNA integrates a simple quadratic interpolation (SQI) to enhance search ability. This study investigates three cases of a typical grid-connected microgrid over 24 hours. The results clearly indicate that the generation cost is minimal when the microgrid actively participates in electricity trading compared to the case where the grid operates passively. Moreover, INNA obtains better results than other methods for all cases, which shows its high performance in finding the optimal generation strategy of the microgrid.

articleTitle: Self-supervised Learning and Masked Language Model for Code-switching Automatic Speech Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Code-switching (CS) is a common linguistic phenomenon that poses significant challenges for automatic speech recognition systems due to the lack of corpus. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to address this challenge by leveraging self-supervised learning (SSL) and the masked language model (MLM) in speech recognition. Specifically, we use the wav2vec 2.0 pre-trained model to reduce the dependency on CS labeled data, and the MLM to rerank sentences generated using beam search decoding. Our proposed method is evaluated on the SEAME dataset, and experimental results show that it outperforms state-of-the-art CS speech recognition approaches by 15.6% and 19.9% in terms of token error rates (TER). Moreover, the proposed method is generalizable and can be extended to other CS languages. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach and its potential for future research in the field of CS speech recognition.

articleTitle: Design of a Rail-to-rail 12-Bit 2.5-MSPS SAR ADC with Low-area on 180nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The Successive Approximation Register Analog-to-digital Converter (SAR ADC) in this research utilizes a simple structure to save area while maintaining good operational performance nearly equivalent to other more complex structures. The SAR ADC was entirely designed based on an analog IC design process, with the digital blocks within this SAR ADC also being implemented at the transistor level for design optimization and area saving. The structure of the single-ended algorithm enhanced the feasibility of the design, especially when designing digital blocks in the analog circuit design process. To address the major drawback of the single-ended SAR ADC, which was rail-to-rail input, the authors also proposed models for the internal components of the SAR ADC. The proposed SAR ADC was implemented on 180nm CMOS process. The SAR ADC had an input range from 439μV to 1.7996V and an output resolution of 12-bit at a sampling rate of 2.5-MS/s and a supply voltage of 1.8V. The ADC achieved a Figure of Merit (FoM) of 989 fJ/Conv.-step due to SNDR of 57.32dB, SFDR of 62.05dB, and 1.486mW power consumption.
