articleTitle: Improve Performance of High-gain Floating Double Series-capacitor Converter with Common Ground and Low-side Gate Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to modify a four-phase double series-capacitor (4P-FDSC) converter. The proposed converter not only inherits all merits of the original converter but also achieves common ground and low-side gate driving for all switches. Only one inductor (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>) and one capacitor (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>) are added, but the extra capacitor helps the output voltage is more stable. And two inductors can couple so that the magnetic volume does not increase. This technique includes several simple modification steps and can be applied to other structures. It is explained step-by-step on the 4P-FDSC converter. A 1.6-kW prototype of the proposed converter was built and tested to verify the performance of the suggested method.

articleTitle: Toward WebTransport Support in HTTP Adaptive Streaming
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Recent years have observed a drastic improvement in video streaming. However, there are still non-trivial open issues that need to be solved, including latency and throughput estimation. In this paper, we present latency improvements to video streaming using WebTransport, a new transport Application Programming Interface (API) for the web platform that enables low-latency, bidirectional communication between web applications and servers. The API is built on top of QUIC, a modern transport protocol that provides low latency, secure, and reliable communication over the internet. By taking advantage of WebTransport’s server push, we present how the latency (e.g., the startup time) of a stream can be decreased compared to HTTP. Furthermore, we propose an efficient way to estimate throughput by leveraging WebTransport, especially for Common Media Application Format (CMAF) low-latency live streaming use cases. The comparisons are conducted with the current version of one of the most popular Dynamic HTTP Adaptive Streaming players, namely dash.js. The goal of these experiments is to identify use cases, where WebTransport could enhance existing dash.js functionality. The experimental results show the outperformance of WebTransport with an improvement of 28% in startup time. Our proposed throughput estimation in WebTransport also presents its ability to detect changes in throughput faster than the conventional technique with acceptable accuracy.

articleTitle: Smart scheduling solutions for home energy management in residential systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As smart grids and renewable energy sources become more prevalent, demand response (DR) has the potential to play an increasingly significant role in balancing demand and supply while also offering economic benefits to consumers. This paper presents an approach to optimal energy scheduling within home energy management (HEM) programs by integrating a DR strategy to reduce electricity costs. The developed model is determined as a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) problem to model smart home devices, including solar photovoltaic (PV) panels, energy storage systems (ESS), electric vehicles (EV), and heating-ventilation-air conditioning (HVAC). By utilizing the MILP model and day-ahead data, the HEM system dynamically adjusts the operations of home devices to reduce daily energy costs. The feasibility of the developed model is demonstrated through a typical smart home, which shows significant improvements in household cost reductions. As a result, DR integration can be a sustainable way to manage household energy consumption, encouraging wider deployment of HEM programs and supporting the transition to a more efficient and resilient power grid.

articleTitle: Inspecting the optical properties of light transmitting concrete for applications in smart traffic
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We proposed and described a vehicle-to-pedestrians (V2P) communication system employing light transmitting concrete (LTC) panel. Additionally, LTC panels made from PMMA optical fibers with different core diameters were also introduced as a key component of the V2P communication system. To ensure that the LTC panel can meet the requirements related to the ability to display the traffic warning signals and observe the information from traffic participants, the optical characteristics of the light transmitting concrete panels were carefully studied in this research.

articleTitle: A Simplified Digital Predictive Current Control for T-Type Three-Phase Three-Level Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Traditional predictive control for T-type three-phase three-level inverters is hindered by laborious weighting factor modification and a significant computational workload, which involve the evaluation of twenty-seven voltage vectors. To address these drawbacks, this article presents a simplified predictive control scheme that omits the need for coefficient weighting. Furthermore, based on the boundary conditions and effects of redundant small voltage vectors, only three candidates of voltage vectors are used to evaluate the cost function, which both relieves the computation burden and achieves neutral-point voltage balance. Finally, a simulation is conducted to authenticate the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Visual Images of Contaminated Objects and Attentional Shift
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Although we expect AI robots for cleaning work to clean the contaminated areas, physically contaminated areas do not always match what we perceive to be contaminated. Thus, to provide us with a more comfortable environment, it is necessary to explore what kinds of objects or situations humans feel contaminated and affect our actual responses, regardless of whether it is physically contaminated. In the present study, we tested whether disgust-related objects affect human attentional systems even when they are presented in artificial environments. Experiments included three tasks: the imaging task, the emotional dot-probe task, and the evaluation task. All tasks were conducted on a computer monitor. In the imaging task, the dish and the animal images were presented on the display. Participants were asked to imagine that the animal was actually on the dish. Next, in the emotional dot-probe task, the target was presented on the display following two dish images. Results showed that responses to the target that was presented on the position of the contaminated dishes were shorter than the target that was presented at the opposite sides of the contaminated dishes. This suggests that, even when the contaminated images are presented on a computer display, it influenced spatial attention, especially automatic attentional shifts. Potential implications for how cognitive and emotional processes affect human behaviors even in artificial environments are discussed.

articleTitle: Digital Baseband Self-Interference Cancellation Using Fractionally-Spaced Finite-Impulse-Response Structure for Full-Duplex MIMO
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this work, a fractionally spaced transversal finite impulse response (FS-FIR) structure is proposed for digital baseband (BB) self-interference cancellation (SIC) in full-duplex (FD) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless communications systems. We develop three algorithms based on Minimum-Mean-Square-Error (MMSE), Least-Square (LS), and Maximum-Likelihood (ML) criteria, to estimate the self-interference channel impulse response and optimize the FS-FIR-SIC coefficients. Performance of the proposed FS-FIR-SIC is evaluated under different oversampling rates and FIR spans. Illustrative results reveal that the FS-FIR structure greatly improves the SIC performance with an oversampling rate larger than 1 by avoiding possible aliasing due to sampling at the symbol rate. Increasing FIR filter span can further enhance the SIC performance, although the improvement is reduced at a large FIR span. Meanwhile, the ML-FS-FIR-SIC outperforms the LS-FS-FIR-SIC and MMSE-FS-FIR-SIC, especially in the presence of the intended received signal.

articleTitle: Improving Human-Object Interaction Detection via Streamlining Matching Procedure and Enhancing Interaction Query
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The domain of Human-Object Interaction (HOI) detection has captured considerable attention within the computer vision research community, given its focus on grasping the action connections between humans and objects. While various methodologies, including sequential, parallel, and end-to-end techniques, have been introduced to address this challenge, recent attention has shifted toward the exploration of end-to-end systems. This paper unveils and addresses the limitations inherent in conventional multi-branch end-to-end methods. Specifically, the output matching process between decoders is identified as a potential source of additional errors in the final predictions. Furthermore, we introduce a novel cross-attention mechanism for human and object representations to mitigate duplication issues in interaction predictions. Our proposed modules are integrated into the HOTR baseline, and experiments show substantial result improvements compared to the original HOTR model. This positions our model competitively among existing methods, as evidenced by evaluations on a widely-used dataset: V-COCO.

articleTitle: A 70dB SNDR Continuous-Time Sigma-Delta Modulator in Sub-GHz Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A low-power second-order continuous-time sigma-delta modulator for analog to digital converter (ADC) in SubGHz transceiver is presented. The modulator is designed in a 55nm CMOS technology. Simulation results show that the modulator achieves 70dB SNDR which corresponds to 11.3 bits ENOB for an OSR of 128 over a 1MHz signal bandwidth. The total power consumption is 2.2mW from a 1.2V supply and the overall active core area is 0.026 mm2.

articleTitle: Higher Order Differential Attack on the Lightweight Block Cipher LBC-3
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: LBC-3 is the lightweight block cipher proposed by Nyssanbayeva et al. in 2022. The block size is 64 bits, the secret key size is 80 bits, and the number of rounds is 20, respectively. The designer investigated the avalanche effect of LBC-3, and Yasushi et al. evaluated the security against differential and linear cryptanalysis. Meanwhile, the security against higher order differential cryptanalysis, one of the most powerful attacks on block cipher, has not been evaluated. In this paper, we evaluated the security of LBC-3 by applying a higher order differential attack. By computer experiments, we discovered the 12-round characteristic using the 28-th order differential. We clarified the reason for this characteristic through a detailed analysis of the nibble values. Then, by using the 60-th order differential, we also show the 18-round characteristic, which is a 6-round extension of the 12-round one theoretically. Exploiting the 18- round characteristic, it is possible to apply the higher order differential attack to full-round LBC-3 with 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">61</sup>'<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> data and times of encryption.

articleTitle: Enhance Radar Performance under Truncated Channel Inversion Transmissions
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The importance of information systems has significantly increased, with research highlighting the benefits of joint radar and communication systems. A joint radar and truncated channel inversion communication system is considered in this work. By adjusting the channel threshold when communication transmission happens, the radar performance can be enhanced while maintaining the communication performance. Our results show that increasing the communication transmission threshold can help increase both radar and communication performance. Our results also show that this threshold can be increased further without affecting communication performance while allowing more available resources to enhance radar performance.

articleTitle: Design of a Cavity Backed Patch Antenna Array for Active Electronically Scanned Array Radar With Wide-Angle Impedance Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A type of cavity patch antenna combined with wide-angle impedance matching (WAIM) method is proposed for Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) Radar. The antenna has wideband, wide-beam characteristics combined with a wide-angle impedance matching method that allows the antenna to scan wide angles while still ensuring active return loss and gain reduction. The simulated results show an active return loss less than −10 dB and gain fluctuation less than 3 dB when steering the beam up to 45° in E plane and 50° in H plane, no grating lobe appears in the entire operating frequency range.

articleTitle: General Coupling Matrix Synthesis for Cruciform Couplers and Its Applications in AFSIW Nolen Matrix Design
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In the advancement of millimeter wave (mmWave) circuits and systems, the air-filled substrate integrated waveguide (AFSIW) stands out thanks to its low loss, low cost, ease of integration, and high performance. Meanwhile, the Nolen matrix represents a beamforming network renowned for its functionalities without the need of cross-overs. In this paper, a 4x4 AFSIW Nolen matrix operating at 28 GHz will be designed using a general synthesis of cruciform couplers with various coupling ratios. Compensating phase shifters are added to mitigate phase errors generated by non-ideal couplers. A good operation was demonstrated through simulation across a 1 GHz bandwidth will all return losses greater than 15 dB and phase differences between two adjacent ports are −45°, 135°, −45°, and −135° with the worst error is 13° at the center frequency. The general synthesis of cruciform couplers simplifies the design of complex beamforming networks with different coupling ratios.

articleTitle: A Split-Merging K-Means Clustering Algorithm with User Attributes for Collaborative Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Collaborative Filtering (CF) stands out as a robust recommendation method that can significantly improve the accuracy of the recommendation system. Nevertheless, conventional CF algorithms face challenges such as cold start and data sparsity. This study presents an approach that combines a split-merging clustering algorithm with user attributes to improve CF performance. Initially, the Split-Merging Clustering (SMKC) algorithm is utilized to cluster users based on their rating vectors, resulting in SMKC. Subsequently, the similarity of the user is calculated by integrating attributes such as age, gender, and occupation to identify the nearest neighbors. Finally, item evaluations are predicted based on user similarities within the nearest-neighbor set to generate the list of recommendations. Experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional approaches in generating recommendation lists, addressing issues related to data sparsity and the inherent cold start in the data.

articleTitle: Towards Integrating Physiological Data in UI/UX Design Learning and Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper introduces an educational framework for incorporating physiological data into engineering classroom activities to enrich the learning process of User Interface/User eXperience (UI/UX) design. Informed by Bloom’s Taxonomy and well-established software engineering design principles, this approach incorporates a variety of key advanced physiological technologies–including eye tracking, palm and fingers movements, brain wave monitoring, muscle movement, and virtual reality–into project-based learning (PBL) scenarios within human-machine interaction (HMI) design. We have analyzed six PBL initiatives in UI/UX design to evaluate the effectiveness of this method. Our findings suggest a transformative shift in engineering education, promoting a more cohesive, data-driven methodology in teaching and learning not only deepens understanding but also stimulates innovation in the field of UI/UX design, particularly within the context of HMIs.

articleTitle: Improve Performance of Dual-output Configuration IPOS Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In renewable applications and DC grids, the bipolar or dual-output loads configuration is preferred due to flexibility, safety, and reliability. Hence, the conventional dual-output input-parallel output-series (IPOS) structure, which has high voltage gain, low switch voltage stress, low input current ripple, and natural output voltage balancing characteristics, is a good candidate. However, the topology still has some minor drawbacks, such as the PWM scheme needing to change when the duty ratio (D) is less than 0.5, leading to complexity in control, and the switch voltage and current waveforms varying through three levels, leading to potential EMI problems. This research introduces a modified IPOS structure, which can solve this problem, and all advantages remain. The switches (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) current stresses reduce when D < 0.5, compared to those of the conventional converter. Furthermore, the capacitor voltage ripples are reduced. The modified converter is verified by simulation and experiments with a 1.6 kW prototype.

articleTitle: In-Band Locating High Delay Variance Links with Programmable Data Plane
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The variation in packet delays, whether occurring on a link or across an end-to-end path, can be precisely quantified as a statistical metric, indicative of the extent of fluctuations in packet delay. Links exhibiting high packet delay variance often signal congestion or instability, making it imperative to identify and monitor such links for effective network performance management. In a prior study, we introduced a method for pinpointing high packet-delay variance links within OpenFlow networks through the use of multicast measurement packets, routed strategically, and by gathering flow statistics of these probe packets from selected OpenFlow switches (OFSs). However, this approach relied passively on the controller-triggered transmission of OpenFlow Flow-Stat packets, leading to delayed detection and response to network events. To address this limitation, our paper proposes a novel scheme leveraging programmable data plane-enabled switches, such as P4-enabled switches, to actively compute packet delay variance and notify the urgent information to the controller. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed scheme in achieving accurate estimation and rapid response to changes in network conditions.

articleTitle: Forward Body Biasing Techniques for Low Power Null Convention Logic in SOI
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Asynchronous circuit design and implementation using Null Convention Logic (NCL) design paradigm, coupled with the inherent benefits of Fully Depleted Silicon on Insulator (FD-SOI) technology, provide a promising path towards efficient and robust digital systems. In this paper, we propose and analyze different circuit design and customization methods for achieving low leakage-power high-performance FDSOI-based asynchronous Null Convention Logic circuits. The basic technique leverages behavior of the fine-grained Forward Body Biasing (FBB) characteristic available in FDSOI transistors to dynamically optimize for low leakage-power or high-performance by adjusting FBB of an NCL circuit using its input Data-Null wave-fronts. Results indicate that, with the addition of extra circuit components with relatively low circuit area, leakage (standby) power is significantly reduced.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Monopolar Patch Antenna Using Modified Ground Plane For 2.4/5.8-GHz WLAN
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A low-profile dual-band monopolar patch antenna with vertically-polarized omnidirectional radiation is presented for 2.4/5.8 GHz wireless local area networks. It is composed of a square ring slot etched on a circular patch, four shorted vias, and a ground plane which are designed to excite TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> modes at 2.4 and 5.8 GHz bands, respectively. In order to broaden the lower band, the ground plane is modified by adding four stubs. The final design with overall size of π×(0.4λ)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>×0.032λ at 2.4 GHz is fabricated and measured. The measurement results show that the antenna achieves impedance matching bandwidths (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| ≤ -8 dB) of 19.6% (2.3 − 2.8 GHz) and 15.4% (5.45 − 6.36 GHz). At two bands, the omnidirectional radiations are yielded with vertical polarization and uniform radiation at the azimuth plane. The peak realized gain of the low band and high band are about 4.0 dBi and 6.81 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Integration of Median Filter and K-means Clustering Technique for Ultrasound Tomography
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Ultrasound tomography is a powerful imaging modality widely employed in medical diagnostics due to its non-invasiveness and small object detection capabilities. However, the reconstructed images often suffer from the presence of noise, compromising the accuracy and interpretability of diagnostic information. In this paper, we propose and evaluate the application of a median filter to address noise artifacts in the reconstructed images obtained through the distorted Born iterative method (DBIM). Quantitative assessment of the proposed approach involves the utilization of evaluation metric, normalized error, to measure its effectiveness. Furthermore, the application of a basic machine learning technique, K-means clustering, assists in automatically dividing the reconstructed image into distinct segments representing objects, background, and noise. The outcomes demonstrate that K-means clustering effectively delineates these regions in images generated through the proposed method, with minimal presence of noise in the recovered images.

articleTitle: Classification of Multiple Incipient Faults in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors under Variable Speed Conditions Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents a classification of multiple faults in permanent magnet synchronous motors at low severity levels under variable speed conditions using a transfer learning-based approach with pre-trained models. The classifier demonstrates the effectiveness of stray flux and current sensors in detecting multiple low-severity faults, specifically local demagnetization and 5% inter-turn short circuit faults. The measured flux data from two locations are converted into spectrogram images using a short-time Fourier transform. A preprocessing method for sequential spectro-images has been developed to mitigate high variance and bias error in training. Within this framework, five pre-trained models from ImageNet are utilized to validate the accuracy and performance at two different sensor locations: ResNet50, VGG16, Inception, Xception, and MobileNet The suggested method is validated with data from an in-house experimental setup.

articleTitle: A Compact Design of Co-Aperture Dual-Sense Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) antenna for simultaneous transmit (Tx) and receive (Rx) communication systems with dual-sense characteristics is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna occupies a 2 × 2 unit-cell metasurface (MS) as the primary radiating aperture, and an asymmetric patch as the CP source of the whole antenna structure. The antenna has two port excitations for dual-CP operation. The final design has compact dimensions of 0.36λ × 0.36λ × 0.02λ (λ is the free-space wavelength at the center operating frequency) with an operating bandwidth of 1.6% (2.45–2.49 GHz). Within this band, the antenna exhibits very high isolation of greater than 32 dB and the peak gain is about 6.0 dBi.

articleTitle: New High Boost DC-DC Converter for Renewable Energy Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-boost power converter for renewable energy systems. The suggested converter exhibits a simplified structure by replacing a diode in the switched-inductor cell with an active power switch to reduce the total voltage stress on the semiconductor device, get cost reduction, and improve efficiency. Additionally, the common ground feature inherent in the introduced topology expands its potential for renewable energy applications. Finally, the simulation verifications are performed using PSIM software to confirm the effectiveness of the suggested approach, and a detailed comparison study between the basic switched-inductor converter and the suggested converter is also presented.

articleTitle: Does the categorization difficulty elicit the uncanny-valley-like phenomenon without animacy?
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We feel strong eeriness for non-human objects that are highly similar to humans (a phenomenon known as uncanny valley). Previous research has accounted for this phenomenon based on animacy perception (e.g., the avoidance to threat or the lack of mind) or cognitive processes irrespective of animacy (categorization difficulty hypothesis). However, whether animacy perception is responsible for uncanny valley to be elicited is unclear at present. This is because all the previous studies used objects related to animacy (creature-like features) as stimuli (e.g., faces). Therefore, the present study examined whether uncanny valley occurs for non-animacy objects, using geometric figures (square, circle, and triangle). In Experiment 1, we made stimulus figures by systematically morphing an original geometrical figure (e.g., circle) into another figure (e.g., triangle). Participants first categorized which original figure (e.g., circle or triangle) the morphed figure was perceived as and then evaluated its likability with a 7-point Likert scale. As the result, we found the uncanny-valley-like phenomenon with non-animacy objects; that is, the figures that took longer times to be categorized (difficult-to-categorize objects) were rated as being less likeable as compared to the figures that were quickly categorized (easy-to-categorize objects). The subsequent experiments hypothesized that the categorization difficulty deteriorates perceptual and cognitive fluency of the morphed figures, resulting in the lower evaluation for them. To assess this hypothesis, we independently manipulated the perceptual (Experiment 2) and cognitive (Experiment 3) fluency of to-be-evaluated figures and investigated how the uncanny-valley-like phenomenon is modulated in response to the processing fluency. The results demonstrated the uncanny-valley-like phenomenon, but no effects of the processing fluency on it. These results suggest that the categorization difficulty is one factor underlying the uncanny-valley-like phenomenon, but the deteriorated processing fluency associated with it does not elicit the phenomenon by itself. We conclude that the uncanny-valley-like phenomenon can be robustly elicited by the stimuli without animacy (or creature-like features), which are in favor with the categorization difficulty hypothesis; that is, animacy perception is not a necessary condition for the occurrence of uncanny valley.

articleTitle: Block Based Focus Volume Pyramid for Shape from Focus
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In shape from focus (SFF), the quality of reconstructed depth map depends on the focus volume (FV) obtained from the image sequence. An FV contains detailed focus information for every pixel in each image of the image sequence and is obtained when a focus measure Operator (FM) is applied on the image sequence. A common issue within FMs is their sensitivity to noise, which can significantly compromise the accuracy of the depth extracted from the FV obtained. To address this, we propose reconstruction of the FV by using a block-based approach. Our approach involves block processing of the FV and then using a statistical measure, the trimean value, for each block to effectively suppress noise. Since the trimean value is independent from the extreme values of the data, it helps in removing the noise. This process is carried out for multiple block sizes, after which we utilize a pyramid approach to aggregate the reconstructed FVs from the varying block sizes, ensuring that no important information is lost from the image sequence. Experiments conducted on both synthetic and real image datasets have proven that our method produces accurate depth maps that are robust to noise.

articleTitle: DSPI - Dual Semantic Parsing Image: A Robust Person Representation for Person Re-Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: One method to significantly enhance the performance of Person-ReID models is to leverage segmentation models to extract semantic parsing information, thus emphasizing the characteristics of human body parts. Studies employing this approach typically utilize CNN architectures as the backbone of Person-ReID, integrating human semantic parsing information into the output of the backbone model, resulting in substantial performance improvement. However, Transformer architectures, utilizing self-attention mechanisms and employing different image data processing techniques from CNN architectures, necessitate a direct integration method for human semantic parsing information into the model’s input. In this study, we propose a novel, simple, and highly adaptable method for integrating human semantic parsing information into input data, called Dual Semantic Parsing Image (DSPI). In this method, a pre-trained segmentation model is employed to extract human pixels from the background and create a new foreground image. The DSPI is formed by horizontally merging the foreground image with the original image, which serves as the input image for the Re-ID model. Our study demonstrates that the Person Re-ID Backbone model ViT+DSPI achieves 93.1% Rank-1 accuracy and 91.1% mAP in the same-domain test of DukeMTMC-ReID, thus attaining state-of-the-art performance. Additionally, significant performance enhancements were observed in cross-domain tests.

articleTitle: High Voltage Gain Floating Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, a high-voltage gain floating boost (HGFB) converter is proposed. In contrast to the traditional interleaved boost converter, the proposed converter attains an increased voltage gain. This enhancement is made possible by the unique structure involving two inductors capable of charging in parallel and discharging in series. As a result, it offers superior performance, especially in applications demanding extremely high conversion ratios. Moreover, the proposed converter's two modules naturally maintain balance without necessitating feedback control, contributing to reduce the converter cost. To confirm the functionality and performance of the suggested converter, simulations were executed at a power level of 1.6 kW.

articleTitle: 3D Hyper-accurate Localization in Indoor Environment for Mobile Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A solution for the three-dimensional (3D) hyper-accurate localization in indoor environment for mobile equipment problem can be based on radar systems. Mobile equipment with an integrated radar system is known as a joint radar-communication (JRC) system or a joint communication and sensing (JCAS) system. The paper proposes an approach for 3D hyper-accurate localization in indoor environment without modifications of cellular network infrastructure. The simulations and experiments show the feasibility of the proposal.

articleTitle: A Compact Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation Method for General Three-phase Multilevel Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents a compact space vector pulse width modulation method for three-phase multi-level inverters. This method helps significantly reduce the workload when programming and controlling the inverters. Test simulation results show that the algorithm works well when applied to general n-level inverters and can even be applied to classic 2-level voltage inverters.

articleTitle: An Active Module to reduce output ripple in power converter
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Output ripple of a power converter is an important parameter and it is desired to be reduced for high quality applications. Traditional filters are bulky and their parasitic elements degrade the performance. Here an Active Module is proposed for parallel connection to a power converter. It can effectively amplify the effective capacitance and suppress the parasitic elements. In this paper analysis is presented and effective result is demonstrated by practical experiment.

articleTitle: An Inverted Approach for Chipless RFID Tag Design Through Parameter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Chipless RFID tag design often encounters challenges due to the mutual coupling effect among resonant components, leading to frequency shifting. This issue is particularly daunting given the need for high capacity and constrained space on a single tag. To tackle this, we introduce a fresh approach merging Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with the empirical Taguchi method (TM). This innovative methodology automates the search for optimal design parameters, ensuring compliance with resonance requirements at specified encoding frequencies. We exemplify this approach through the design process of an I-shaped slot tag structure, showcasing its effectiveness in resolving mutual coupling challenges.

articleTitle: Carrier-Based PWM Method for Output Capacitor Voltage Balancing of Vienna Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study examines the control mechanism and DC neutral point balancing of a three-phase, three-wire, three-level Vienna rectifier utilising the carrier-based pulse width modulation approach. This method increases the quality of the input current and DC capacitor voltage by detecting irregular intervals without having to know the position of the reference vector. Given the operating parameters, the compensating components for the three phases are computed based on the unbalanced factor and added to the controller's modulation ratio. Therefore, the voltage imbalance between the DC capacitors is decreased. The suggested model includes a control method that uses CB-PWM implementation to provide simple and effective neutral-point voltage regulation.

articleTitle: Towards 6G xURLLC with Non-orthogonal HARQ
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The demand for the neXt generation Ultra-Reliable and Low-Latency Communications (xURLLC) poses unprecedented challenges in the design of 6G wireless networks. Hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) is the most popular error-control method to enhance the system’s reliability at the cost of increased latency due to the retransmission of erroneous packets. To meet xURLLC requirements, this paper presents an enhanced non-orthogonal HARQ (N-HARQ) scheme inspired by non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) technology. Notably, the NHARQ scheme enables simultaneous redundancy retransmission and new packet transmission within a shared time slot in a non-orthogonal fashion. Moreover, unlike conventional approaches, the proposed N-HARQ scheme incorporates a "waiting" state to effectively utilize system resources during severe fading channel conditions. Different performance metrics, including achievable throughput, average packet delay, and system efficiency, are analytically derived based on a Markov model. Numerical results highlight the effectiveness of our proposed N-HARQ over the state-of-the-art. Also, the correctness of the analytical model is verified by Monte-Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: A Novel NoC-based SNN Architecture with Optimized Routers
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), with their efficient energy usage, have gained prominence in AI hardware inference tasks. One of the major challenges regarding the implementation of SNN using a Network-on-Chip (NoC) architecture is the handling of packet routing, a mechanism to send and receive packets among the neuron cores of the network. For many of the proposed SNN NoC-based architectures, the routing components are integrated inside cores, which leads to significant resource consumption and latency issues, particularly in large-scale net-works. This paper addresses these challenges by introducing a novel NoC-based SNN architecture, in which routers are externalized outside of the cores, each linked to four adjacent cores and surrounding routers in the network grid. This approach helps to reduce resources significantly in large networks, in which the number of routers takes up a considerable proportion. Specifically, our approach results in the hardware resource reduction of 17.88% Look-Up Table and 36.91% Flip-flops. This also leads to a 5.68% decrease in the power consumption.

articleTitle: Communication Attack Analysis of Multi-Agent System over Wide-Area Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study focuses on attack analysis on communication link within a wide-area network. The multiple groups that make up this network are isolated from one another. An agent that is present in every group and can communicate with other leaders at discrete times over a strongly connected directed graph is called a leader. Analyzing the impact of communication link attacks on the wide-area network’s consensus mechanism is our goal here. By applying concepts from matrix theory and graph theory, we demonstrate how a single attack on a communication channel could disrupt the consensus control law. Simulations are used to demonstrate the findings of our study.

articleTitle: DConvT: Deep Convolution-Transformer Network Utilizing Multi-scale Temporal Attention for Speech Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Transformers have made significant progress in a wide range of speech processing tasks. However, they are not widely explored in real-time speech enhancement due to the complex distribution of noise over speech signal in challenging scenarios. Pure transformers can hardly capture the structure of speech harmonics and how they change over time in the noisy speech spectrogram. To fill the gap, we propose a deep convolution-transformer network (DConvT), in which the multi-scale temporal attention is designed to effectively model different speech structures from multiple temporal scales in a convolutional encoder-decoder architecture. In DConvT, multi-scale temporal information is extracted by dilated convolutions and projected to the query/key-value sequence of the self-attention operation. In this way, the self-attention can perform global modeling on a variety of temporal structures separately. The multi-scale temporal attention results are subsequently merged by concatenation to fuse the information of multiple temporal patterns. In addition, we adopt a convolutional encoder-decoder (CED) architecture to efficiently model and down-sample the frequency dimension of the speech spectrogram, which produces compact sequences for temporal modeling. The experimental results on 2020 Deep Noise Suppression Challenge (DNS20) dataset show that DConvT achieves state-of-the-art performance among existing speech enhancement baselines.

articleTitle: Dual-Purpose Saltwater Structure: EMI Shielding Window and UHF Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a transparent structure that serves as a dual-function device - an adjustable antenna with an electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding window. This design achieves transparency (>91%) by using salt-water with a conductivity of 20 S/m inside regular glass, providing it to operate as an optical window. The glass structure with saltwater function as C-band EMI shielding window with shielding efficiency (SE) of more than 20 dB. To adjust the frequency and beam direction, the antenna with dual-port feeding configuration operates at UHF frequency range. The measurement outcomes indicate a bandwidth with range from 350 to 680 MHz and a radiation efficiency exceeding 60% for a basic single-port feeding distribution setup. In comparison to the basic setup, the additional configuration with two-port feeding of the same power and phase adjustment offers tunable frequency, tunable radiation, and better gain. These results highlight the flexibility of the proposed antenna, which serves as both an EMI shielding window and a tunable antenna.

articleTitle: Food Intake Detection in the Face of Limited Sensor Signal Annotations
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Food Intake Detection from wearable sensor signals is essential in applications like dietary monitoring. Traditional annotation methods for sensor datasets are notably labor-intensive and time-consuming. Addressing this, our paper presents a novel methodology that employs a denoising convolutional autoencoder trained on an extensive unannotated dataset to extract key discriminative features from the sensor data. Subsequently, a small, selectively annotated subset of this dataset is utilized to train a LightGBM classifier. The classifier leverages the features extracted by the autoencoder to distinguish between eating and non-eating events effectively. Our research utilizes the AIM-2 sensor system, equipped with a 3D accelerometer and an optical sensor mounted on eyeglasses to monitor muscle movement and head motion. Data was collected from 17 participants, each wearing eyeglasses for varying durations. For validating the LightGBM classifier, a cross-validation method was used where the data from each participant was used once as a test set, and the data from eight randomly selected others formed the training set. Repeated for each participant, this approach ensured individual data contribution to the validation. The final performance metrics, calculated as an average across all participants, demonstrated robust results with an F1 score of 83.71%, a specificity of 88.43%, and a sensitivity of 86.26%. These performance metrics underscore the efficacy of our approach, which significantly reduces the need for extensive data annotation.

articleTitle: A Wearable BTE-EEG Embedded Device for Emotion Monitoring with Quantum Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Emotional disorders present significant challenges in both mental health research and clinical practice, underscoring the critical need for effective recognition and intervention strategies. This study introduces a groundbreaking approach that employs a behind-the-ear (BTE) EEG system for emotion recognition, utilizing quantum machine learning techniques. The research encompasses a comprehensive design framework addressing both hardware and software aspects of the BTE-EEG emotion recognition system for data acquisition and monitoring. By utilizing BTE-EEG technology, this study aims to improve comfort, mobility, and signal quality compared to traditional scalp EEGs, thus enabling continuous monitoring in real-world settings. Furthermore, the integration of quantum computing and machine learning represents a paradigm shift in emotion recognition and cognitive tasks, offering exponential speedups and superior pattern recognition capabilities compared to classical approaches. The findings underscore the efficacy of the proposed BTE EEG system in accurately detecting emotional states (positive and negative). This advancement shows promise for enhancing our understanding of emotional disorders and improving clinical interventions tailored to individual needs.

articleTitle: Impulsive Noise Resilient Mean Shift Filtering for Effective Color Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The degradation of color images caused by noise significantly diminishes their quality. Consequently, enhancing noisy images becomes a pivotal step in the processing pipeline. In this paper, we present an extension of the widely used Mean Shift (MS) technique. While MS efficiently handles Gaussian noise, it falls short in reducing impulsive noise. Our proposal involves the application of a robust similarity measure between a pixel and the central patch of the processing block. This measure is resilient to the influence of impulsive noise, addressing a limitation of MS. To mitigate the impact of corrupted pixels in the block centered at the pixel being restored, we assign a measure of pixel’s impulsiveness. This ensures that noisy pixels carry significantly less weight in the iterative MS process.The combination of the robust pixel-to-patch similarity measure with the degree of pixel corruption enables overcoming impulsive disturbances, allowing for the application of the MS technique in suppressing mixed Gaussian and impulsive noise. The proposed technique can serve as a preprocessing step for segmentation, edge detection, and object recognition.

articleTitle: Cooperative Control of Multi-Connected Autonomous Vehicles: Dynamic Event-Triggered Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In many applications, such as atmospheric observation or disaster monitoring, coordinating motion control of a group of autonomous vehicles is crucial because it is effective in repetitive task execution. In this paper, we consider the dynamic event-triggered cooperative control for multi-autonomous vehicle subjected to the resource-constrained vehicle such as energy, communication constraints. The dynamic event-triggering approach to nonlinear multiple autonomous vehicles is proposed, which is based on internal dynamic variables. Our advanced approach is compared to current triggering laws via internal dynamic variable. Finally, the numerical simulations will be given to illustrate the effectiveness of our theoretical results.

articleTitle: Preserving Power Optimizations Across the High Level Synthesis of Distinct Application-Specific Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We evaluate the use of software interpretation to push High Level Synthesis of application-specific accelerators toward a higher level of abstraction. Our methodology is supported by a formal power consumption model that computes the power consumption of accelerator components, accurately predicting the power consumption on new designs from prior optimization estimations. We demonstrate how our approach simplifies the re-use of power optimizations across distinct designs, by leveraging the higher level of design abstraction, using two accelerators representative of the robotics domain, implemented through the Bambu High Level Synthesis tool. Results support the research hypothesis, achieving predictions accurate within ±1%.

articleTitle: An Implementation of IoT System for Collecting Vibration Signals of Ships Engines to Support Engine Failures Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The paper presents the implementation of an IoT (Internet of Things) device to monitor and to detect abnormal states of ship engines based on vibration signals. The system uses components such as ESP32, ADXL335 GY-61 accelerometer sensor, DS18B20 temperature sensor, and HiveMQ MQTT Cloud for storing and displaying real-time data of ship engines. With technological advancements, vibration signals can be leveraged as an efficient and cost-effective approach for detecting faults. The article focuses on collecting vibration data from sensors placed on the engine, then using signal analysis techniques to identify signs of faults. Experimental findings show that this monitoring and alert system enhances the performance and safety of ship engines by facilitating early detection of potential issues or malfunctions in engine operations. Additionally, machine learning technology will be integrated to classify errors collected by this system.

articleTitle: A Novel Skewed Permanent Magnet Technique for Improving Performances of SPMSMs with Outer Rotor Type
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motors (SPMSMs) are extensively used in industrial applications because of their exceptional performance, dependability, and versatility in terms of shapes and sizes. There are two primary types of SPMSM based on the construction of the rotor: SPMSM with inner rotor configuration and SPMSM with outer rotor configuration. In this context, a skewed permanent magnet (PM) technique is proposed to improve performances of the SPMSM with outer rotor type, such as improvement of back electromagnetic force and reduction of cogging torque. The novel approach allows to use multiple slices of PMs with different angles instead of applying with a single slice as in the previous studies. The computation process is approached with both analytical background and finite element analysis (FEA). Where the analytical model is first established to determine essential parameters of the machine, the FEA is finally developed to compute and simulate electromagnetic parameters based on the analytical results. The development of both method are verified on the practical SPMSM of 5.5kW.

articleTitle: A proposed Power Converter for an AC Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The paper proposes a novel structure of an AC Battery with a two-stage topology. The Three-port converter (TPC) is proposed for the DC/DC stage to connect with multiple voltage standards of the second-lifetime batteries. The Four-Leg converter is proposed for the DC/AC stage to flexibly operate both with the single-phase and three-phase grid or load. Additionally, a control structure for the proposed AC Battery is presented. Finally, the operating principle of a three-phase AC Battery is validated through Matlab/Simulink simulations. The simulation results show the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed AC Battery

articleTitle: Winding Function Model for Detecting Demagnetization in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) are widely used in electromechanical actuators and energy systems, thus always work in dynamic operations, and expose external stresses in hash environments. Under such stresses, the PMSM might face challenges of overloading under high currents or voltage, and vibration from the environment, resulting in demagnetization fault in the rotor and inter-turn short circuit fault in the stator winding. This paper presents an analytical model for the faulty machine based on improved winding function theory. The model could be used to formulate the characteristic frequencies associated with the faults. These frequencies could be used as the indicator for incipient fault detection systems. The developed model is numerically verified and experimentally validated from an in-house experimental setup.

articleTitle: Joint Pilot and Data Power Optimization in Cell-free Massive MIMO Systems using Heterogeneous Graph Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Pilot contamination caused by the reuse of pilot sequences poses a significant challenge in cell-free massive MIMO systems. The problem can be mitigated by the optimization of pilot power to enhance channel estimation. In this paper, we propose a max-min achievable uplink rate optimization problem to jointly optimize powers allocated to pilots and data across all users. To tackle the intricate non-convex problem, we present a novel architecture based on a heterogeneous graph convolutional network. Simulation results demonstrate superior performance of our proposed algorithm compared to conventional approaches.

articleTitle: Decentralized Multilevel Inverters based on CPWM for Five-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents a new structure and implementation method of a multilevel decentralized control power converter for a 5-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor (5PMSM). Decentralized carrier level shift modulation technique is used to search for switching pulses for each phase power switches. The proposed structure and control method allows the power converter to operate under normal conditions and any one phase or two phases open circuit of the 5PMSM. The 5PMSM is controlled based on rotor field-oriented control (RFOC) on d-q coordinates to ensure that the motor’s electromagnetic moment ripples with the low amplitude. The feedback of the stator current and motor speed is used to adjust the current on the d-q coordinate to create a modulation voltage for each phase. The speed response, electromagnetic moment, phase voltage, phase current, carrier modulation process are analyzed and evaluated based on the simulation model on the Matlab/Simulink software.

articleTitle: Enhanced Bit-Rate Performance for Visible Light Communication Systems Between Led and Mobile Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Multiple Pulse Position Modulation (MPPM) has become an important method in optical communication, especially between LEDs and mobile cameras. This paper proposes an MPPM modulation and demodulation method for Visible Light Communication (VLC) systems using LED bulbs and the camera for the transceiver that addresses data transmission performance barriers when increasing the distance between receiver and transmitter, as well as helps minimize comparison error rates compared with other modulation techniques. The PPM and MPPM modulation methods are both highly rated for their power and bandwidth efficiency. Using binary codes and image data processing algorithms at the receiver, along with optimized mapping, aids in minimizing character errors and enhancing communication performance. Additionally, integrating MPPM into the VLC system solves the problem of brightness control in real-world scenarios. The MPPM-based brightness control system is capable of dynamically adjusting brightness, providing higher communication performance and stability for the VLC system.

articleTitle: Design of A Compact Sequentially-Fed Metasurface-Based Patch Antenna with Wide Bandwidth And Circularly Polarized Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a design of wideband circularly polarized microstrip patch antenna that has compact dimensions. To achieve broadband and circular polarization properties, the proposed antenna employs sequential-phase (SP) feeding networks and 4 arrays of 2 x 2 unit-cell metasurface. The overall sizes of the proposed design are 1.02 λ0 x 1.02 λ0 x 0.05 λ0, in which λ0 is the free space wavelength at the center frequency of 5.0 GHz. Simulation results indicate that the impedance and axial ratio bandwidths of the SP-fed MS-based antenna are 27.6% and 22%, respectively. In addition, the proposed design produces a high peak gain of 10.9 dBi. In comparison with the related works, the antenna in this paper offers good performance with relatively wide CP operation bandwidth and high gain while maintaining a fairly compact dimensions.

articleTitle: A Study of the Fast Current Protection Method for the Silicon-Carbide (SiC) MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Power converters play a critical role in almost all applications, particularly in medium and high-power fields where semiconductors must withstand high current and voltage conditions. Consequently, implementing effective protection methods against overcurrent and short circuit faults is imperative. The desaturation method has emerged as a widely utilized approach, especially with Si IGBT. However, applying this method to SiC MOSFETs poses challenges due to limitations in response time. Thus, a thorough analysis of the desaturation method for SiC MOSFETs is warranted. This paper elucidates the operational principles of desaturation, conducting simulations utilizing LT-Spice XVII with real element models. Additionally, experimental results employing the gate driver IC NCV57000 from ON-Semiconductor are presented to validate the methodologies and findings.

articleTitle: Meet-in-the-middle Cryptanalysis of IVLBC
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: IVLBC is a lightweight block cipher proposed by Xiantong Huang et al. in 2023. IVLBC consists of a 64-bit block of 28 rounds with an 80/128-bit key. In the paper written by a third party, differential and linear cryptanalysis of IVLBC were already reported, but the Meet-in-the-middle (MITM) attack on IVLBC has not been reported yet. Therefore, we study the MITM attack on IVLBC from a third- party standpoint. This paper shows the MITM attack on IVLBC consisting of 8 rounds. We first search for the characteristics used for the MITM attack on IVLBC. Then, we show that 8 rounds of IVLBC-80 are vulnerable to MITM attack with 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">75</sup>·<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">547</sup> times of encryption operation and 4 plaintext-ciphertext pairs. In addition, we show that 8 rounds of IVLBC-128 are also vulnerable to MITM attack with 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">116</sup>·<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">541</sup> times of encryption operation and 6 plaintext-ciphertext pairs. Our study shows the best results among single-key attacks performed by third parties.

articleTitle: A Design of 10 – 16 GHz CMOS High Spectral Purity Frequency Quadrupler
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a frequency quadrupler operating in the 10-16 GHz range using 65-nm CMOS technology. The quadrupler comprises two cascaded push-pull doublers (PPD) and two 1-bit elliptic bandpass filters (BPF) for harmonic filtering. The interleaved BPFs effectively suppress undesired harmonics, resulting in a high harmonic rejection ratio (HRR). Measurement results demonstrate a worst-case output HRR exceeding 27 dBc across the 10-16 GHz frequency range with an input power of 2.5 dBm. The quadrupler exhibits a minimum conversion loss of 3.8 dB, corresponding to a maximum output power of -1.3 dBm. The chip occupying an area of 1.89 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> consumes 65 mW with a 1.2 V power supply.

articleTitle: A Straightforward Deadbeat Control Scheme for Three-phase Voltage Source Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Conventional finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) methods are well-known for their variable switching frequency, leading to noise and significant voltage and current ripple. Based on model predictive control, this study introduces a straightforward deadbeat control method with a constant switching frequency for a voltage source inverter, in order to provide a modulated waveform at the output of the converter. The proposed method achieves fast dynamic response since the load current tracks the reference current after two sampling intervals. The practicality of this technique is assessed through simulation results that emphasize the positive attributes of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Meet-in-the-Middle Attack on the 15-Round Variant of the Lightweight Block Cipher Shakey for Protection of IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper applies Meet-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks to Shakey [3]. Shakey is the lightweight block cipher for Internet of Things (IoT) applications proposed by Anushka Sivakumar et al. in 2023. It features a 128-bit secret key, 32 rounds of iterative function, and a 64-bit block size. The structure of Shakey is a Generalized Feistel Network (GFN) and Addition Rotation XOR (ARX) network. While the paper proposing Shakey assessed only differential attacks, no evaluation using MITM attacks, proposed by Diffie and Hellman in 1977 [6], has been conducted. This investigation applies MITM attacks on Shakey, demonstrating that the maximum number of attackable rounds is 15. The attack requires less than 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">128</sup> times of Shakey encryption operation –— specifically 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">126.600</sup> and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">126.596</sup> times of an encryption operation–, three and sixty-five known plaintext-ciphertext pairs, respectively, and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">126</sup> words of memory.

articleTitle: Design of Circularly Polarized 1-Bit Reconfigurable ME-Dipole Reflectarray for C-band
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel electronically reconfigurable reflectarray antenna (RRA) having circular polarization (CP) for C-band communications (4.4 - 5 GHz). The RRA is designed using a magnetoelectric (ME) dipole element combined with four PIN diode elements. This configuration enables flexible control over the phase of the CP reflected wave from each pixel, ensuring precise manipulation of the main reflected beam direction. A 10×10 reflectarray prototype was validated through numerical analysis, showcasing its capability for two-dimensional (2-D) beam scanning. Notably, the proposed RRA structure achieves wide beam-scanning angles up to ±60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> with a scanning loss of 4 dB and a 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of 9.28% (4.52 - 4.96 GHz). Hence, the proposed RRA structure is an effective method for enhancing wireless communication signals on mobile terminals.

articleTitle: A Novel True Wireless Stereo Communication Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: True Wireless Stereo (TWS) communications are notably impacted by the fading channel caused by wireless signal over a human body. In this paper, we introduce a novel technique for TWS communication system. This method enables the relaying earbud to simultaneously transmit signals along with the smartphone, allowing the receiving earbud to capture two signals concurrently at different frequencies. Through comprehensive theoretical analysis and rigorous simulation studies, we demonstrate that our novel technique outperforms traditional methods.

articleTitle: Prototype Design of Real-Time OFDM Transceiver in 300-GHz Band for Backhaul Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: With the expanded spectrum allocation as specified in RR5.564A, the 300-GHz band facilitates the development of high-capacity backhaul solutions for fixed services, utilizing its broadband capabilities in the context of 6G communications. The authors have focused on high-efficiency transmission surpassing that of single-carrier systems, culminating in the completion of a prototype OFDM transceiver equipment for proof-of-concept purposes. This paper presents the design of each block comprising the RF front-end, which includes a power amplifier and mixer circuit utilizing InP-based high-electron-mobility transistors within the 300-GHz band, 47 dBi lens horn antenna, a low-loss dielectric multi-layer multi-element patch antenna for beam-forming and a wideband baseband for amplitude and phase compensation in multicarrier modulation. Furthermore, results from demonstrative experiments are discussed.

articleTitle: Predictive Power Control for T-Type Nested Neutral Point Clamped Inverter Without Weighting Factor and Reduced Computational Burden
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper offers a simplified method for direct power control employing model predictive control (MPC) for a four-level T-type Nested Neutral Point Clamped inverter-connected grid. A discrete-time model is used to forecast the grid current and power for evaluating the cost function. Unlike the traditional MPC, which utilizes exhaustive searches for all viable switching combinations, the proposed method only considers the possible candidates based on the needed inverter voltage sector for the optimization loop during the initial stage. During the second phase, the redundant switching status, which is considered the best output vector, will be employed to balance the capacitor voltages. Therefore, the computation load is not only dramatically reduced but also eliminated the weighting factors tuning by the suggested approach. The proposed method’s efficacy is substantiated through comparative simulation studies conducted under both steady-state and dynamic-state operations.

Author Keywords: T-type Nested Neutral Point Clamped inverter

articleTitle: A Flexible Residual Neural Network for Rician Noise Removal in MR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Rician noise removal is a crucial problem for processing magnetic resonance (MR) images. In this paper, we present a flexible residual neural network (FDnResNet) for Rician noise reduction. The proposed model employs noise level map to improve modeling capacity and to adjust the compromise between noise removal and image feature preservation. Additionally, our model uses residual blocks to enhance the information flow between the shallower and deeper layers in the network. The experimental results of FDnResNet on simulated brain MR image database demonstrate the superiority of our proposed residual neural network utilizing noise level map.

articleTitle: 50-dB Attenuation Range 3-bit Low Insertion Loss Ku-Band and Ka-Band 100nm GaAs Digital Step Attenuators
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents 50-dB attenuation range low insertion loss 100nm Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) digital step attenuators at the Ku-band and Ka-band. The distributed type, combined with parallel RC compensation and reduced-size quarter-wavelength techniques, is utilized to achieve low insertion loss, good attenuation, and phase error. Specifically, the 14-18 GHz DSA exhibits an insertion loss of less than 4.8 dB and a Root-Mean-Square (RMS) amplitude error of 0.72 dB. Similarly, the 34-37 GHz DSA achieves an insertion loss of under 6.4 dB and RMS amplitude error of 1.14 dB. The output third-order intercept point (OIP3) of both designs is approximately 40 dBm.

articleTitle: Immunosensor Based on Printed Circuit Board for Protein Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Nowadays, many electrochemical immunosensors have emerged, tailored to specific applications by customizing commercial electrodes. The electrode surface was modified to attach specific antibodies, enabling the capture and detection of antigens through physical measurement techniques. In this paper, we developed a simple and low-cost electrochemical immunosensor based on the printed circuit board (PCB) platform for protein detection. The proposed immunosensor configuration was designed using CAD software and fabricated on FR4 substrate, a commonly used material in printed circuit boards. Subsequently, a thin layer of gold was applied over the copper layer to create a metal substrate. The electrode shape can be easily designed and fabricated to the desired shape using this approach. The electrode surface modification process was carried out to facilitate the binding of the antibody to the gold substrate. A round-shaped gold layer with a diameter of 3 mm was fabricated on the PCB, and an electrochemical sensor configuration with a parallel structure was designed. This configuration comprised two PCBs structured with gold electrodes placed in parallel, maintaining a distance of 5 mm between the two electrodes. This configuration allowed for convenient sensor usage. The working electrode was separated from the counter electrode to mitigate potential negative effects during the surface modification process. Experiment results have demonstrated the sensor can detect the 5 µM bovine serum albumin (BSA). The presence of BSA was verified by both fluorescent images under the microscope and impedance measurements. With achieved results, the proposed immunosensor configuration shows promising potential for low-cost and easy fabrication in bio-detection applications.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition using Wireless Signals and Low-Cost Embedded Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Developing affordable and privacy-aware smart home applications remains a challenge. Existing camera-based and sensor-based solutions often raise concerns about cost and user privacy. This paper proposes a low-cost WiFi-based sensing system utilizing ESP32 microcontrollers and Jetson Nano edge devices for human activity recognition (HAR) within smart homes. The system captures Channel State Information (CSI) data using an ESP32-based WiFi transmitter and receiver, eliminating the need for expensive hardware while ensuring privacy preservation. A mix of conventional machine learning and deep learning models are evaluated on the obtained dataset, achieving an accuracy of up to 95.57%. The best-performing model is then deployed on the Jetson Nano edge device for efficient activity classification and high throughput. Furthermore, the system seamlessly integrates with existing communication protocols such as Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT), and provides a user-friendly interface for visualization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by achieving accurate HAR using a single transmitter-receiver pair, highlighting its practicality and scalability potential. This work aims to further exploration of WiFi sensing technology for smart home applications by enabling cost-effective and privacy-preserving HAR.

articleTitle: Accelerating Network Slice Embedding with Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Network slicing plays an important role in next-generation communication systems (5G and beyond). With network slicing, mobile network operator is able to create various logical networks (slices) that are tailored to support specific services. One of the most challenging problems in network slicing is how to share the physical resources across multiple slices in an efficient way. This paper proposes some heuristics based on reinforcement learning to effectively solve this sharing problem. Simulations have been performed to evaluate the proposed methods, in comparison with exact solutions obtained from solving an integer linear program. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed learning-based algorithms in solving the problem of network slice embedding.

articleTitle: A Novel Paradigm Shift for Next-Generation: Symbiotic Backscatter Rate-Splitting Multiple Access Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Next-generation wireless networks are projected to empower a broad range of Internet-of-things (IoT) applications and services with extreme data rates, posing new challenges in delivering large-scale connectivity at a low cost to current communication paradigms. Rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) is one of the most spotlight nominees, conceived to address spectrum scarcity while reaching massive connectivity. Meanwhile, symbiotic communication is said to be an inexpensive way to realize future IoT on a large scale. To reach the goal of spectrum efficiency improvement and low energy consumption, we merge these advances by means of introducing a novel paradigm shift, called symbiotic backscatter RSMA, for the next generation. Specifically, we first establish the way to operate the symbiotic system to assist the readers in apprehending the proposed paradigm, then guide detailed design in beamforming weights with four potential gain-control (GC) strategies for enhancing symbiotic communication, and finally provide an information-theoretic framework using a new metric, called symbiotic outage probability (SOP) to characterize the proposed system performance. Through numerical result experiments, we show that the developed framework can accurately predict the actual SOP and the efficacy of the proposed GC strategies in improving the SOP performance.

articleTitle: Joint Latency Minimization and Power Allocation for MEC-Enabled MU-MISO Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study investigates the Quality of Experience (QoE) for the user equipment (UE) at the network edge in a multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) system. In this paper, a novel edge computing model which involves both offloading and local execution time is first introduced. Then we formulate a QoE fairness problem, aiming to minimize the system computational latency. To tackle this optimization challenge, we propose an approach based on convex approximation that accounts for constraints related to offloading ratios and power allocation. Finally, we present numerical findings that validate our theoretical framework and showcase the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Sum-Rate Maximization in Hybrid Beamforming Multi-User Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This work develops deep reinforcement learning (RL)-based techniques to perform power allocation in hybrid beamforming (HB) multi-user massive multiple-input multiple-output (MU-mMIMO) systems. We aim to maximize the achievable system sum-rate constrained to a total transmit power limit. The optimization problem is non-convex and solved in three main steps. First, a radio frequency (RF) beamformer is designed based on the slow time-varying angle of departure (AoD) information of users. Second, a baseband (BB) precoder is derived based on regularized zero-forcing technique using the lower-dimensional effective channel state information (CSI) seen from the BB stage. Afterward, the power allocation (PA) task is formulated in the reinforcement learning framework and it is solved by two main approaches: (i) single-agent deep Q-learning (SA-DQL), (ii) multi-agent deep Q-learning (MA-DQL). An RL agent learns to choose an action (i.e., PA block/value) that maximizes its expected cumulative reward (i.e., sum-rate) through interactions with the environment.
