It is shown that SA-DQL-based PA can closely approach the performance of exhaustive search in terms of achieved sum-rate and performs significantly better than the MA-DQL-based PA and equal PA scenarios.

articleTitle: WiLHPE: WiFi-enabled Lightweight Channel Frequency Dynamic Convolution for HPE Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Recently, there has been significant attention to WiFi-based human pose estimation (HPE) within the research community due to its device-free nature, cost-effectiveness, and privacy preservation. The implementation of such a solution requires improved model performance while upholding efficiency, particularly when employing resource-constrained devices. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel approach, the so-called WiLHPE, which integrates multi-modal sensors such as cameras and WiFi to accurately detect human pose landmarks. WiLHPE involves processing the raw WiFi signal through a novel neural network architecture to dynamically learn convolutional kernels weighted with attention across channel and frequency kernel spaces. This innovative approach diversifies the kernels to enhance the recognition capabilities of WiFi signals without introducing additional complexity, thus guaranteeing efficiency. Results conducted on the MM-Fi dataset underscore the superiority of WiLHPE over state-of-the-art approaches, all while ensuring minimal computational overhead. This makes the proposed approach highly suitable for large-scale scenarios.

articleTitle: Improvement of Vietnamese noun phrases chunking in text-based person image search
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Natural language processing is a crucial and beneficial task in various multimedia processing applications. Text-based person search (TBPS) application involves finding person images in an image gallery using an input as a text sentence. Previous studies have shown that noun phrases is one of the most important components in person description sentence as users employ noun phrases to describe the person characteristics. However, in recent TBPS the noun phrase chunking mainly bases on some set of rules. Low quality noun phrase chunking may lead to irrelevant results of text-based person search. In this paper, a method for Vietnamese noun phrase chunking named VNPC (Vietnamese Noun Phrase Chunking) is proposed. The method is based on Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) model and it is improved with a task-dependent post processing ruler to be integrated in Vietnamese text-based person image search framework. Compared to the Vietnamese Noun Phrase Chunking based on Conditional Random Fields [14] using only simple CRFs, which achieved an average recall and precision of 82.72% and 82.62% respectively, we achieved better results in chunking (with the same dataset splitting ratio). Experimental results show that the proposed method allows to obtain a high quality noun phrase chunking performance with 88.02%, 90.09%, and 89.01% of Precision, Recall, F1 score. And it helps to improve the person search results in TBPS by 1.325%, 0.675% and 0.25%, of accuracies at the top-1, top-5 at the top-10 respectively.

articleTitle: Mobile Subscriber Location Estimation based on Logistic Regression for Enhancement of Paging Procedure in 5G and beyond Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Mobility management in mobile networks is challenging, especially when the number of UEs is numerous and the moving patterns are diversified. It demands fresh approaches to minimize signaling overhead and maintaining service quality requirements. Mobile network operations generate vast data, and exploiting insights from big data with machine learning techniques is a strategy for operators to improve the efficiency of the operational system. This work introduces the logistic regression algorithm to predict the states of User Equipment (UE) based on its movement history and the paging policies adapt with the UEs states. The mechanism is proposed under the thorough investigation of data logs of mobile users operating data services of a mobile service provider in Vietnam. Evaluated with the data set of real mobile users, the results illustrate the improvement in the paging process, the participation of radio base stations in the paging procedure can be reduced by approximately 95%, while still maintaining a paging success ratio of over 95%, which is the required level of the mobile service provider.

articleTitle: Effective Consensus Computation for Public Blockchain in Small-World Network Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes effective methods to find the optimal scale-related parameters of the Small-World Network to minimize the speed of solving consensus problems in public blockchains. We demonstrated that the consensus problem is worked out quickly on specific small-world networks with an average shortest path between nodes. An effective algorithm is proposed to find the network model of N nodes possessing good consensus convergence time such as the maximum degree, the average path length, and the large vertex and edge connectivity. A relationship between the topological properties of networks and a randomly rewiring probability β is also shown. This way, the average shortest path length is dynamically calculated to get high-speed spreading of consensus time.

articleTitle: BER Performance of Downlink MIMO-NOMA with Combination of SFBC and Joint Maximum-Likelihood Detector
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Reducing the influence of multipath channels and simplifying the equalizer at receivers are the main benefits of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM). In this paper, we take advantage of OFDM to implement downlink multipleinput multiple-output (MIMO) non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems under the view of space-frequency block code (SFBC). In particular, we implement a combination of SFBC at a base station and a joint maximum-likelihood (JML) detector at two users to improve the bit-error-rate (BER) performance. For evaluating the system’s performance, we mathematically obtain closed-form approximate expressions of the BER performance and the maximum diversity gain for two users on Rayleigh fading channels under the assumption of a small number of channel taps. Through computer simulations, we validate that analytical results match quite well with simulation results and asymptotic results in the low and high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regimes, respectively. Based on expressions of BER, the fairness problem of the system is considered, and it shows that the power allocation for achieving justice becomes inconsequential when both the transmit power and the number of receive antennas are sufficiently large.

articleTitle: Flyback Converter Transformer Design Optimization by AI
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The paper proposes an AI converter design method to cope with high power density requirements based on the Bayesian Optimization (BO) algorithm, aiming to achieve high-efficiency selection of converter parameters. An active clamp flyback (ACF) converter with 240W output power is taken as an example, the application effect of the BO algorithm in actual converter design is introduced in detail. The research process covers key steps such as initialization, transformer characteristic simulation, circuit simulation, transformer core loss simulation, efficiency calculation, and BO algorithm iterative optimization. The BO algorithm takes efficiency as the objective function and performs 10 ~ 20 iterative optimizations to obtain the best efficiency value. The experimental results verified the reliability of the simulation results and further confirmed the practical application value of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Expanding Vision in Tree Counting: Novel Ground Truth Generation and Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Manual labor in tree management is expensive and not efficient enough to track changes in the number and distribution of trees in a large area. Recent methods focus on automatic counting using deep-learning networks, in particular density map-based methods, in aerial images. This research introduces two contributions: a new ground truth generation practice to boost the training effectiveness by minimizing the loss of labeled trees in the target density maps; and a combination of a Vision Transformer (ViT) and a dilated convolutional neural network (CNN), termed TreeVision, to generate high-quality density maps. The combination of these two methodologies provides us with high-quality ground truths to extract rich contextual information by the global self-attention performed by ViT and a large receptive field of dilated convolutions. Empirically, both of our proposals yield positive results, in particular, better performance of models trained in the updated ground truth and state-of-the-art results when evaluating TreeVision on two benchmark tree-counting datasets (Yosemite and KCL-London). Our TreeVision delivers a 9.29% lower Mean Absolute Error (MAE) in the KCL-London dataset and competitive results in the Yosemite dataset in comparison with previous leading methods.

articleTitle: Optical-Flow and Human-Segmentation Based Method for High Accuracy Detection of Golf Swing Key Events
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Golf swing sequencing is a crucial aspect of golf performance analysis, requiring precise identification of key events throughout the swing motion. Traditional methods for analyzing golf swings face limitations in accuracy and efficiency, prompting the exploration of AI-driven solutions. In this paper, we propose a novel method that integrates golfers’ movement obtained from human segmentation with optical flow, along with whole frame analysis to enhance the accuracy of key event detection in golf swing videos. The proposed approach utilizes a pipeline consisting of human segmentation, optical flow, feature extraction, and classification to detect key events in the golf swing. Additionally, various data augmentation techniques are employed to enrich the training dataset. Therefore, our research improves model generalization and performance. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method, achieving a Percentage of Correct Events (PCE) of 82.2% on the GolfDB dataset, a promising result compared to SwingNet.

articleTitle: Pubic Symphysis-Fetal Head Segmentation in Ultrasound Images with Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Pubic symphysis-fetal head (PS-FH) segmentation is a crucial task for measuring the angle of progression (AoP) of the fetal head during labor, which is an objective and reliable parameter that reflects the fetal descent and the likelihood of vaginal delivery. However, manual segmentation of PS-FH from transperineal ultrasound (TPU) images is time-consuming, subjective, and prone to inter-observer variability. Therefore, automatic PS-FH segmentation methods based on deep neural networks have been proposed to improve the efficiency and accuracy of AoP measurement. In this paper, we survey different loss functions, U-Net backbones, and attention mechanisms for PS-FH segmentation, and compare their performance on a public dataset. We have found that the combination of U-Net, EfficientNet, IoU loss, and scSE attention achieves the best performance, with an average accuracy of 0.96, an average Dice score of 0.96, and an average IoU of 0.93. This demonstrates the effectiveness of our method, which can extract more effective features from the ultrasound images, while optimizing the overlap ratio between the predicted and ground truth masks, and enhancing the feature maps by recalibrating the channel-wise and spatial-wise importance.

articleTitle: PeanutAD: A Real-World Dataset for Anomaly Detection in Agricultural Product Processing Line
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Anomaly detection in production lines - automatically detecting defects in product processes - plays a vital role across several domains. Several industrial anomaly detection datasets have been built with severe challenges to overcome. However, the need for more amount and diversity of training data in specific systems in the real world, especially in agricultural product processing lines, remains to be considered. In this work, we introduce a peanut anomaly detection dataset (PeanutAD), a real-world dataset for anomaly detection tasks, reflecting the actual conditions in production lines. Experiments on this dataset demonstrated significant room for improvement because of some challenges. With PeanutAD, we aim to expand the anomaly detection database quantitatively and qualitatively, allowing researchers to further enhance and evaluate anomaly detection techniques with the most realistic setup possible. PeanutAD and experimental results on baseline methods shall be kept fully open-source as a contribution to the research community <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>.

articleTitle: A method for missing joint recovery and its application in skeleton-based activity recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The recognition of human activities is a crucial problem in computer vision, aiming to determine the activities of individuals or groups based on a sequence of images or videos. While previous studies have demonstrated feasible results in activity recognition from skeletal joints, challenges arise in conditions with occlusion, complex motions, and inaccurate joint estimations, leading to missing joints that can impact the effectiveness of subsequent recognition steps. This paper proposes a method for recovering missing joints in the estimation of human joints from motion in videos and applying it to activity recognition. With the proposed method, the results of the model’s 3D space estimation with missing joints show great potential, although the model still exhibits some weaknesses in challenging scenarios. For the activity recognition task, the recognition results of the DD-Net model on the Mica-Action3D dataset have improved by up to 25%.

articleTitle: Exploiting Machine Learning And Gene Expression Analysis in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Despite many research efforts, the biological insight related to Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), a rare disease resulting in the loss of motor neurons and causing mortality, remains elusive and leads to challenges to the diagnosis of the disease. Fortunately, gene expression data has recently appeared as a potential approach for the functionality analysis of genes related to orphan diseases and for providing more accurate diagnosis outcomes. Moreover, with the explosion of machine learning (ML), implementing ML in analyzing biomedical data has become a promising direction with a notable effect on our lives. Leveraging these advantages, in this paper, we investigate to shed light on the effects of gene markers on ALS diagnosis and propose a novel gene combination that is effective in ALS diagnosis. We retrieve the datasets and perform the cleaning and pre-processing methods to obtain robust data for analysis. Then, the Max-Min Parents and Children (MMPC) and Sequential Forward Feature Selection (SFFS) algorithms are applied to achieve the optimal gene subsets that are effective for the final intelligent diagnosis model. Notably, the coefficient of the Ridge Classifier is utilized as the crucial score for determining the gene importance ranking table based on the selected gene signatures. All the possible gene combinations are evaluated and optimized in a set of robust machine learning algorithms. Consequently, a set of 20 genes identified through the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm is selected as the optimal for the ALS diagnosis with an accuracy of 88.30% and an AUC score of 91.11%, which is dominant in comparison with notable traditional methods under the same datasets.

articleTitle: Classification of Electroencephalography Signals with Auditory Stimuli using Complex Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Electroencephalography signals serve as valuable tools for studying the human brain activity and detecting various neurological disorders. This study proposes a novel approach to analyze electroencephalography signals in response to auditory stimuli and language variations utilizing Visibility Graph and Horizontal Visibility Graph algorithms, with and without segmentation. By extracting statistical properties and fitting the degree distribution of the networks, a feature vector is obtained for classification problems using k-nearest neighbor and support vector machine algorithms. Analysis results indicated that the Horizontal Visibility Graph outperformed the VG, whereas segmentation methods showing minimal impact on the classification performance. Moreover, the support vector machine classifiers demonstrate stable performance, and achieve average accuracy of nearly 60% to over 70% through 10-fold cross-validation. This proposed method is the foundation for further studies of pattern classification with EEG signals.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis for Rotating Machine Utilizing Machine Learning with FFT-based Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Rotating machines have an important role in industrial production which requires a regular scheduled service and routine checks. Any unexpected failures can result in significant financial losses and personnel damage. Thus, fault diagnosis is crucial. Among the common types of faults, unbalanced and misalignment which cause the high vibration levels are rarely studied. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for fault diagnosis using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) for extracting features from a collected dataset of vibration signals. Several machine learning models are utilized for training after applying feature extraction such as Random Forest (RF), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and Xtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Based on the outcomes of various tests, Random Forest has outperformed the others in the frequency range of 30Hz-40Hz, with an accuracy of 91.14%.

articleTitle: An Extended OVN Architecture for End-to-End QoS Guarantee in Network Slicing
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, Network Slicing has emerged as a solution to help deploy services with different Quality of Service (QoS) requirements on the same shared physical infrastructure. To facilitate resource allocation in network slices, a Virtual Infrastructure Manager (VIM), e.g. OpenStack or Kubernetes can be used to virtualize and manage the physical infrastructure. Currently, Open Virtual Network (OVN) is one of the main open-source technologies used in the above VIMs to create virtual networks and deploy network slices. However, these VIMs are only capable of managing overlay network infrastructure built on compute nodes that are directly connected through tunneling protocols and Virtual Tunnel Endpoint (VTEP). OVN can therefore only control traffic at the endpoints of the virtual link (VL). As a result, end-to-end QoS for services deployed on virtual networks created by OVN cannot be guaranteed on shared network node infrastructure. This paper proposes a solution based on a traffic tagging mechanism to bridge this gap of OVN and develops an architecture based on SDN/OVN integration to manage QoS for network slices dynamically. Then, the performance of the proposed architecture is evaluated through specific use cases.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Optimization for Federated Learning in Cell-free Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, federated learning (FL), a promising machine learning technique, has gained increasing attention. Unlike traditional approaches that centralize data for training a global model, FL enables model training to occur on user devices (UEs), prioritizing data privacy and security. A key challenge in implementing FL over wireless communication lies in optimizing the energy efficiency of user devices, especially considering their limited power resources. In this paper, we address the problem of minimizing total energy consumption during the training phase of FL in a cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output system. The optimization problem is formulated with the goal of minimizing the overall energy consumption of all UEs during the FL training process. To address the nonconvex and intricate problem, we propose an iterative algorithm utilizing the inner approximation method. This approach transforms the problem into a series of successive convex problems, yielding at least one locally optimal solution. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in addressing the given problem. The results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed approach compared with benchmark algorithms.

articleTitle: Advancing Cryptographic Security: A Study on SHA-3 Implementation within CRYSTAL-KYBER Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Hardware
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As quantum computing advances, it introduces profound risks to the security of cryptographic communications. Current cryptographic technologies, though advanced, fall short of quantum resistance. This research investigates the potential of lattice-based cryptography, specifically CRYSTALS-KYBER, to fulfill this need through superior performance and security. We present the hardware implementation of cryptographic primitives optimized for parallel operation in terms of area and frequency. These primitives, adhering to the SHA-3 standard and designed for KEM-768 level 3 security, have been synthesized to operate at 400 MHz frequency over a 130,069 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area using TSMC 65-nm technology. The implementation on Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA and subsequent comparative analysis establish our methodology's efficacy in advancing quantum-resistant cryptographic solutions.

articleTitle: CS-TE Abstraction Framework: Ballet Teaching, Training, and Testing Station with Kinect Sensors and EEG Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This article advocates the use of abstraction in the design of a standardized ballet learning, training, and testing station. The framework could also be applied to other types of dancing as well. On the one hand, the state-of-the-art engineering research approach focuses on mathematical models, algorithm, complexity, and efficiency of gesture recognition processes. On the other hand, our approach is top-down, where lower-level abstraction inherits the concepts from the upper-level. And the very top-level concepts are in accordance with how dancing artists really think while they generate their work of arts.

articleTitle: Efficient Resource Allocation Framework for Network Slicing-enabled Open RAN
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The transition to 5G technology has revolutionized cellular networks, leading to an unprecedented demand for high-bandwidth and low-latency services. To meet these evolving demands, next-generation mobile networks are turning to innovative solutions such as network slicing within the open radio access network (RAN) architecture. This paper focuses on addressing the challenges associated with dynamic virtual network function (VNF) mapping and resource allocation in terms of both communication and computing resources. The ultimate goal is to simultaneously maximize the total reward for admitted slices and minimize the associated cost by allocating resources to the Open RAN slices catering to diverse service types. To efficiently solve the formulated problem, we decompose it into two sub-problems tailored to different timescales which are executed at the different layers within the Open RAN architecture. To solve the non-convex long-term problem, we first transform it to a more tractable form and employ the successive convex approximation (SCA) method to achieve at least a locally optimal solution. Numerical simulations demonstrate the efficacy and quick convergence of the proposed algorithm, highlighting its potential to improve network slicing performance and support diverse applications in future wireless networks.

articleTitle: A study on natural language processing-based method for Windows malware detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study focuses on applying Natural Language Processing (NLP) in Windows malware detection to address the complex problem of classifying and detecting diverse malware patterns. The proposed method combines both static and dynamic malware attributes, using NLP to analyze and understand linguistic characteristics within the malware. By using readable strings and API sequences from analyzed results as inputs to a deep learning multimodal, our proposed method can achieve a high accuracy of 0.99 for the classification task and 0.96 accuracy for the time-based detection task. The combination of static features like strings and dynamic attributes such as API sequences, along with the use of NLP, provides a comprehensive and effective approach to detecting malware in a practical environment.

articleTitle: Weighted Fusion Architecture for Improved Ovarian Tumor Segmentation from Ultrasound Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Ovarian tumor segmentation is a challenging task that requires high accuracy. This study presents a novel method for improving binary segmentation in ovarian ultrasound imaging by using a weighted fusion approach. This strategy utilizes a grid search algorithm to optimize the weights for fusing segmented maps from different models, achieving higher Precision and Recall. We investigated 3 backbone architectures, including Inceptionv3, DenseNet121, and MobileNet within the UNet framework - renowned for its effectiveness in ultrasound imaging, to generate a fused heatmap. In addition to this, MobileNet was then adopted as the backbone across two other different segmentation models: FPN and PSPNet due to its efficiency and high performance, followed by a similar weighted fusion approach together with UNet for the final predicted mask. Our findings show significant improvements in all key metrics, including Precision, Recall, IoU, and F1 Score, over individual methods.

articleTitle: Accuracy and Speed Improvement of Lidar Inertial Odometry and Mapping by using Gravity Estimation and Incremental Voxels
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: LiDAR-inertial fusion-based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is becoming increasingly important for enabling autonomous vehicles and mobile robots to perceive and localize themselves within unknown environments. Currently, two predominant tightly-coupled LiDAR-inertial Odometry (LIO) methods are widely used: filter-based and graph-based optimization. While the former is faster, the latter is more accurate. LIO-SAM, known as one of the state-of-the-art graph-based optimization methods, still assumes that the gravity vector remains constant, affecting the accuracy of pose estimation. Additionally, it requires high computational resources, especially for large-scale environments, which causes slower runtime per scan. In this paper, based on conventional LIO-SAM algorithm, we propose an enhanced LiDAR-inertial SLAM framework to solve the above issues. We integrate gravity estimation for better IMU motion prediction, resulting in improved pose estimation. Furthermore, we adopt the incremental voxels (iVox) data structure to replace traditional K-Dimensional tree, resulting in better runtime performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed framework provides reasonable improvements about 30% in terms of both pose estimation accuracy and average runtime per scan.

articleTitle: Stream Cipher Using Chaotic Maps for Secure Multimedia Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents a pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) using two-dimensional chaotic maps, called the chaos-based PRNG. The proposed PRNG generates a secure key stream. According to important properties of the discretized Cat and Standard maps, combining a nonlinearized permutation layer on bits and a linear mixing layer on bytes effectively creates pseudo-random number sequences. The stream cipher from the chaos-based PRNG is an effective alternative for low-complexity encryption of sensitive information in multimedia data. Encryption is performed in the video slices and images, where an identified Region Of Interest (ROI) is encrypted. The results obtained from the practical tests indicate the robustness of the proposed stream cipher.

articleTitle: QoD aware Energy Efficient Active RIS-assisted Multi-User Multi-Stream Precoding by Scalable Complex Iterations
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The paper provides the first investigation on energy efficiency (EE) in delivering multi-stream information to multiple multi-antenna users using an active reconfigurable intelligent surface (aRIS)-assisted system. We proposed the joint design of the transmit precoders and of the aRIS’s quantized power-amplified reconfigurable elements (APREs) to maximize the ratio of geometric mean (GM) log-det to power consumption. A new computationally efficient alternating descent algorithm based on closed-form expressions is developed. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can achieve both high EE and minimum log-det rate.

articleTitle: Minimizing Energy Consumption in Mobile Robotics with STAR-RIS in Smart Factories
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The integration of robots into networks, forming connected robots, holds great promise as the technology for upcoming smart factories. These robots offer cost-effective solutions and demonstrate exceptional maneuverability. However, the stability and quality requirements of communication links between the access point (AP) and the robots pose issues that restrict their applicability in factory environments. These limitations arise especially in scenarios where obstacles may obstruct wireless connections. To tackle these issues, we propose a system that adopts a Simultaneously Transmitting and Reflecting Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (STAR-RIS) to improve connectivity between the AP and the robot. Subsequently, we formulate an optimization problem that seeks to enhance the robot’s trajectory, optimize the transmitted power of the AP, and the transmission and reflection amplitude and phase shift of the STAR-RIS. The goal is to minimize the total energy consumption of the system while ensuring compliance with obstacle avoidance constraints and meeting the required data rate threshold. We efficiently solve this joint optimization problem using a deep reinforcement learning method. Simulation results showcase the efficacy of our proposed system and algorithm, particularly in terms of energy efficiency and robot movement within smart factory environments.

articleTitle: Toward an AI-embedded capsule endoscopy system for medical healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Automated computer-aided techniques for detecting colorectal polyps in capsule endoscope images present a promising avenue for enhancing the post-processing phase of endoscopy, thereby assisting healthcare professionals with increased accuracy. A notable challenge lies in the absence of precise localization information, hindering physicians' ability to precisely identify the location of detected polyps for subsequent procedures such as screening or removal. In this research, we present an innovative electronic system for capsule endoscope localization, along with an AI-powered recognition model, aimed at integrating into an active locomotion system for the automatic detection and localization of colorectal polyps. The active capsule endoscope system consists of a magnetic capsule endoscope (MCE) and a magnetic actuation device capable of controlling the MCE's movement in five degrees of freedom. A deep learning model is employed for automatic detection of colorectal polyps with high precision. The localization device incorporates a 2D array of magnetic sensors and acquisition electronic circuits to measure the magnetic signal emitted by the MCE. The capsule's precise position in five degrees of freedom is determined using an optimization algorithm. Upon polyp detection, the MCE’s location is recorded alongside the captured image of the detected polyp, facilitating historical analysis and aiding in subsequent examinations. While this study primarily focuses on extracting information related to colorectal polyps, the proposed method has the potential to be expanded for detecting abnormalities throughout the entire digestive tract.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Precoding and Probabilistic Constellation Shaping for Physical Layer Security in Visible Light Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The inherent broadcast nature of the light signal requires robust security solutions against eavesdropping attacks for visible light communications (VLC). Aside from conventional cryptography, physical layer security (PLS) is a novel paradigm to protect information confidentiality. This paper proposes a joint design of precoding and probabilistic constellation shaping (PCS) for enhancing the performance of PLS in multiple-input single-output (MISO) VLC systems. Specifically, the proposed design aims to optimize the secrecy capacity while ensuring the reliability of the channel of the legitimate user. The optimal design is shown to be a non-linear and non-convex problem that is difficult to solve using classical optimization techniques. Therefore, a hybrid particle swarm optimization (PSO) and genetic algorithm (GA) are employed to tackle the problem. Simulation results demonstrate that compared with the precoding-only design, the proposed joint design achieves a better secrecy capacity (especially at the low optical power region) and can guarantee the reliability of the legitimate user’s channel over the examined optical power region.

articleTitle: Empowering Federated Learning with DDPG for Energy Efficiency in Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of allocating energy-efficient transmission and computation resources for federated learning (FL) across wireless communication networks. In the FL model we investigate, each user computes limited local computational resources to train a local FL model with its collected data. Subsequently, the trained FL model is sent to a base station (BS), which aggregates the local FL models and broadcasts the resulting model back to all users. Because FL entails exchanging a learning model between users and the BS, computation, and communication latencies are contingent on the level of learning accuracy. Additionally, due to the wireless users’ constrained energy budgets, we should consider both local computation energy and transmission energy during the FL process. We formulate the challenge of learning process and communication as an optimization task to minimize the overall energy consumption of the system while adhering to a latency constraint. To address this problem, we investigate an iterative algorithm wherein closed-form solutions for resource allocation with latency, bandwidth, transmit power, computation frequency, and learning accuracy are derived at each step. Given that the iterative algorithm necessitates an initial feasible solution, we apply a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based algorithm. The results demonstrate our work can reduce total energy consumption by up to 65% compared to other DRL agents.

articleTitle: Development of a Compact System Integrating Pre-Concentrator and Electrochemical Measurements for Protein Pre-Concentration and Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study presents the research and development of an embedded system integrating a pre-concentrator and an electrochemical measurement circuit for the concentration and detection of proteins in a microfluidic chip. The system is composed of five main blocks, namely the central control unit, measurement circuit, voltage controller, bio-chip, and graphical user interface (GUI). After the design, the system was fabricated using the multilayer layer printed circuit board (PCB) and monolithic aluminum processing techniques. Additionally, embedded software was developed for the microcontroller, and a graphical user interface (GUI) was created for screen interaction, facilitating the execution of system functions. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system is capable of generating output voltages ranging from 15 V to 90 V with a response time of 300 ms. The pre-concentrator functioned effectively in both depletion and enrichment modes using bovine serum albumin–fluorescein isothiocyanate conjugate (BSA-FITC). Notably, in the enrichment mode, the fluorescence intensity of the concentration zone increased from 28 A.U to 55 A.U after seven minutes. Moreover, cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements were conducted using standard redox solution and Randles equivalent circuit, respectively. The measurement results closely resembled those obtained from commercial devices, affirming the system's performance and reliability. In the future, a point-of-care testing system can be developed for protein quantification and cancer diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Unified Framework for Plant Identification from UAV Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) with their ability to capture imagery at various spatial and temporal scales offer significant potential for applications in plant identification and biodiversity monitoring. In this paper, we propose a unified framework for plant identification from UAV images comprising three components: orthomosaic image construction, plant segmentation, and plant identification. First, orthomosaic images are generated from images captured by UAVs using OpenDroneMap. Then, these images are segmented into forest, deforestation, and other areas. Finally, image patches that are extracted from forest regions are fed into plant identification to determine the plant species. Extensive experiments were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of each component on a self-collected dataset captured from Ben En National Park in Thanhhoa province. Preliminary results demonstrate the potential application of UAVs in biodiversity mapping.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Deployment Models for Microservices in an Edge-based Serverless Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In the edge computing ecosystem, microservices and serverless computing are gaining attention recently. The first one provides a highly flexible and scalable software design, while the latter offers a resource efficiency mechanism for running software, promising for IoT deployment at the edge. However, microservices, mainly deployed by Kubernetes (K8s) – a container orchestration platform, has intrinsic overhead, which is potentially exacerbated by the container/pod layer introduced by K8s. This problem, while can be negligible in the cloud, might be significantly limited in terms of capabilities in edge environments. To this end, this article investigates the impacts of different deployment types, namely native, container, and pod, for microservices in various categories: resource consumption, performance, availability, and scalability. The results show quantitative measurements of the mentioned metrics and, in particular, also the advantages and disadvantages of each deployment type for developers to design their microservices efficiently.

articleTitle: Enhancing Continual Abdominal Multi-Organ and Tumor Segmentation through Best Model Knowledge Distillation and Encoder-Decoder Training
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Continual learning is crucial for medical image segmentation tasks, as it enables the extension of recognition capabilities to accommodate the expansion of data and classes without compromising privacy and security. Motivated by the need for more efficient and effective continual learning models in medical image segmentation, we propose a novel model that builds upon the work of Zhang et al. (2023) while introducing notable improvements. Our model utilizes two novel techniques to enhance continual learning performance. First, we aggregate additional information from the decoder during the model training phase to improve the model’s representational capacity. Second, we propose an effective knowledge distillation method that leverages the knowledge from previously trained models to generate pseudo-labels for new data, thereby eliminating the need to access old data. This approach effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting while complying with privacy and security constraints. We evaluate our proposed method on the benchmark BTCV dataset and compare its performance against several baseline methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms some of the baseline methods in certain instances, showcasing the effectiveness of our dynamic architecture expansion, decoder information aggregation, and knowledge distillation techniques. Our findings pave the way for further research in developing efficient and effective continual learning methods for medical image segmentation.

articleTitle: Implementing Convolutional Auto Encoder on FPGA using High Level Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study introduces a CNN-based Autoencoder implementation on FPGA using High-Level Synthesis (HLS), focusing on optimizing convolutional computing for reduced latency and enhanced resource efficiency. Implemented on the FPGA, the design utilizes 69,407 Flip-Flops (FFs), 104,467 Look-Up Tables (LUTs), and 3,716 Digital Signal Processors (DSPs), achieving an operational frequency of 100 MHz and a latency of 0.15 milliseconds. Through techniques such as pipelining, parallelization, and loop unrolling, we navigate the balance between resource utilization, computational speed, and image reconstruction fidelity. Our findings demonstrate the potential of HLS for efficiently deploying deep learning models on hard-ware, offering valuable insights for advancements in real-time processing applications.

articleTitle: Resource-Constrained Intelligent Trap: Fruit Flies Surveillance Framework with TinyML Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The threat posed by fruit flies to fruit crops requires innovative solutions to protect the harvest. Our research introduces an advanced solution to safeguard fruit crops from the menace of fruit flies using the ESP-EYE microcontroller and the FOMO algorithm with Edge Impulse AI Platform. Our intelligent insect trap is equipped with advanced features and demonstrates excellent performance. With a maximum RAM usage of 2.4Mb and an inference time of 5.694 seconds, the device achieves an impressive 96 percent accuracy based on the Intersection over the Union threshold (IoU) of 0.5. This effective solution not only ensures professional detection and count capabilities but also provides timely notifications to farmers about potential threats. It enables the use of targeted pesticides use in regions with high fruit flies, minimizing widespread spraying, and ensuring efficient crop protection. Furthermore, the trap runs smoothly without human intervention, thanks to its automatic replacement feature for fly-stained adhesive traps. This sustainable approach, adaptable to various types of pests, improves resource utilization and productivity, underscoring its significant value in agriculture and other related fields.

articleTitle: Enhancing Supervised-Learning Fault Classification of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors with Feature Selections
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Inter turn short circuit (ITSC) faults in the permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) using applied signal processing methods might not be detected at low severities or in early stage. Four supervised machine learning (ML) algorithms, namely decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGB), and support vector machine (SVM) are used to classify different incipient faults with the healthy condition. Phase current datasets of an in-house PMSM are collected in the healthy, 2% ITSC, and 5% ITSC fault conditions. Statistical features, namely root mean square (RMS) crest, impulse, kurtosis, standard deviation, are calculated based on the measured data for the classification. Wrapper-based feature selection (WFS) technique is employed to optimize the best features to maximize the classification accuracy while reducing computational complexity. It is found that the combination of RMS factor, standard deviation, and crest factor is the best feature for fault classifications of 2% ITSC and 5% ITSC.

articleTitle: PBDM: Peak-Based Differential Method for Improve Leg Detection Performance with Laser Range Finder
publicationTitle: 2024 Tenth International Conference on Communications and Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Determining human presence is crucial for robots engaged in complex tasks such as avoiding and tracking obstacles. Incorporating diverse sensors in robots poses challenges and opportunities to enhance detection algorithms, which rely on the diversity of input signals for recognition. Modern methods for differentiating lower limbs use laser rangefinder signals, segmenting regions believed to be legs, and identifying distinctive features based on geometric and spatial properties of the data. This study introduces the Peak-Based Differential Method (PBDM) to improve the accuracy and efficiency of segmentation by identifying potential pins through analysis of signal peaks in one-dimensional (1D) space. Then, five specific features of human legs are described and extracted from these segments in two-dimensional (2D) signal space for object classification. The implementation of this innovative method aims to optimize the overall accuracy of the detection process, reduce the number of features needed for accurate identification, and reduce processing time. Implementation of these methodological improvements has shown promising results when applied in real-life scenarios, highlighting their potential effectiveness for complex robotics applications.
